builds.name: Sword & Shield
builds.goal: Balanced frontline anchor: reliable damage with a solid guard.
builds.requires: STR, a shield, medium–heavy armour.
builds.downside: Master of none — out-damaged by 2H, out-tanked by Pure Tank.

builds.name: Axe & Shield
builds.goal: Shield-breaker: strip an enemy shield, then cut.
builds.requires: STR, an axe (bonus shield damage), a shield.
builds.downside: Lower raw damage than swords once the shield is gone.

builds.name: Mace & Shield
builds.goal: Anti-armour control: stun / knockdown and dent armour.
builds.requires: STR, a mace (2nd-best armour damage + stun), a shield.
builds.downside: Wasted on unarmoured foes; modest cutting damage.

builds.name: Cleaver & Shield
builds.goal: Bleed-and-crit bruiser behind a shield.
builds.requires: STR, a cleaver (high bleed/crit), a shield.
builds.downside: High stamina drain; bleed is slow against armour.

builds.name: Flail & Shield
builds.goal: Ignore the enemy guard and hit weak spots (top precision).
builds.requires: STR, a flail (highest weakspot precision + stun), a shield.
builds.downside: Erratic, lower base damage than swords/axes.

builds.name: Spear & Shield
builds.goal: Defensive anti-flanker: reach + knockback holds a line.
builds.requires: STR, a spear (reach, knockback at tier), a shield.
builds.downside: Low damage — a holder/support, not a killer.

builds.name: Sword (Duelist)
builds.goal: High-tempo 1H swordsman: faster and more precise than 2H, no shield.
builds.requires: High DEX + dodge, the Duelist trait, light–medium armour, a free off-hand.
builds.downside: Fragile (no shield, light armour); heavy armour caps its speed.

builds.name: Axe (Duelist)
builds.goal: Duel-grip axe: fast shield-splitting with a free off-hand bonus.
builds.requires: High DEX + dodge, the Duelist trait, light–medium armour.
builds.downside: Fragile; loses the shield-break value against unshielded foes.

builds.name: Mace (Duelist)
builds.goal: Fast duel-grip stun: precise blunt control, no shield.
builds.requires: High DEX + dodge, the Duelist trait, light–medium armour.
builds.downside: Low damage on unarmoured foes; fragile.

builds.name: Cleaver (Duelist)
builds.goal: Fast bleed duelist: high crit + bleed with a free off-hand.
builds.requires: High DEX + dodge, the Duelist trait, light–medium armour.
builds.downside: Stamina hungry; fragile.

builds.name: Flail (Duelist)
builds.goal: Duel-grip flail: weak-spot hunter that ignores the guard.
builds.requires: High DEX + dodge, the Duelist trait, light–medium armour.
builds.downside: Erratic damage; fragile.

builds.name: Spear (Duelist)
builds.goal: Reach duelist: keep distance, poke and knock back, no shield.
builds.requires: High DEX + dodge, the Duelist trait, light–medium armour.
builds.downside: Low damage; very exposed once closed on.

builds.name: Greatsword (2H)
builds.goal: Cleaving frontline that punishes crowds (AoE swings).
builds.requires: STR, a 2H sword, room to swing.
builds.downside: No shield, slow, stamina-heavy.

builds.name: 2H Cleaver
builds.goal: Maximum bleed, crit and raw cutting damage.
builds.requires: STR and a deep stamina pool.
builds.downside: Highest stamina drain of any weapon; slow.

builds.name: 2H Axe
builds.goal: Shield-destroyer with armour-damage AoE.
builds.requires: STR, a 2H axe (devastating shield damage).
builds.downside: Slow; no shield; less raw damage than the greatsword.

builds.name: 2H Hammer
builds.goal: Armour-crusher and boss-breaker: top armour-durability damage + stun/knockdown.
builds.requires: STR, a 2H hammer/maul.
builds.downside: Slow; poor against unarmoured foes; no shield.

builds.name: Polearm (2H)
builds.goal: Backline reach + the highest knockback; anti-flank spacing.
builds.requires: STR, a rank behind the front line.
builds.downside: 2H slow, less precise; weak once an enemy closes.

builds.name: Pure Tank
builds.goal: Unkillable anchor that soaks hits and provokes enemies onto itself.
builds.requires: Heaviest armour + heaviest shield, high CON, taunt/provoke traits, a stamina-cheap weapon.
builds.downside: Negligible damage — a wall, not a threat.

builds.name: Fencer (Rapier)
builds.goal: Precision duelist: the highest precision, armour-piercing thrusts.
builds.requires: PER (finesse), light–medium armour, a rapier/estoc.
builds.downside: Low raw damage; fragile.

builds.name: Assassin (Dagger)
builds.goal: Fastest attacker; bypass armour and backstab from stealth.
builds.requires: DEX, low encumbrance, stealth, a dagger.
builds.downside: Tiny per-hit damage without position; very fragile.

builds.name: Archer (Bow)
builds.goal: Longest-range precision fire with the best ranged crit.
builds.requires: PER, high skill, a clear line, arrows.
builds.downside: Needs the most skill; helpless in melee.

builds.name: Crossbowman
builds.goal: Armour-piercing ranged with a low skill floor.
builds.requires: PER, bolts.
builds.downside: Shorter range than a bow; slow reload.

builds.name: Skirmisher (Throwing)
builds.goal: Close-range harasser with the highest AP and armour damage of the ranged builds.
builds.requires: STR/PER, a stock of thrown weapons.
builds.downside: Shortest range; limited ammo.

builds.name: Slinger (Sling)
builds.goal: Cheapest, fastest-firing chip damage; easiest to land.
builds.requires: Minimal skill, stones.
builds.downside: Lowest damage / AP / armour damage; blunt only.

builds.name: Battlemage (1H Staff)
builds.goal: Elemental caster that keeps a shield or off-hand: massive per-shot damage, unlimited ammo.
builds.requires: INT, a 1H staff, stamina management.
builds.downside: Slow, huge stamina per shot (Magic Drained); frail.

builds.name: War-Caster (2H Staff)
builds.goal: 2H elemental staff that doubles as a high-stun blunt weapon.
builds.requires: INT, a 2H staff, stamina.
builds.downside: Slow; Magic Drained on overuse; no off-hand.

builds.name: Stunwaller (2H Staff)
builds.goal: Non-magical allrounder: best blunt precision + fastest attack to stun-wall with weak pawns.
builds.requires: A 2H staff; very low stat bar to use.
builds.downside: Lowest damage / AP / armour damage — pure control, no kills.

objects.name: Campfire
objects.desc: A simple fire pit. Provides warmth, cooking, and a place for colonists to gather food. Requires fuel and lighting.

objects.name: Stone Hearth
objects.desc: A stone-ringed hearth, a lasting fire. Cooks, boils water, throws light, dries firewood stored nearby, and warms an enclosed home. The heart of a settled colony. Built from any loose rock.

objects.name: Bare Craft Spot
objects.desc: A designated area where a pawn squats to knap stone and weave fiber. No structure, just intent.

objects.name: Branch Workbench
objects.desc: A rough workbench lashed together from your first tools, planks laid flat, wedged and bound with cordage. A real working surface, a step up from knapping on the ground: it crafts the same primitive recipes faster and unlocks composite tools, leather work, and clay containers.

objects.name: Butcher Spot
objects.desc: A sturdy branch lashed between two posts with a hook for hanging carcasses. Process kills into meat, hide, and bone.

objects.name: Granite Dressing Slab
objects.desc: A flat slab of dressed stone set on hewn log stakes, with a hanging rail and bone-chip drainage groove. Yields 25% more from each carcass than the raw butcher spot.

objects.name: Bear Rug
objects.desc: A whole bear pelt, head and claws left on, spread before the hearth. Softens a floor and makes a hall of a hut.

objects.name: Trophy Mount
objects.desc: Antler, tusk or great fang set on a carved board. Every guest hears the story of the hunt whether they ask or not.

objects.name: Dire Wolf Rug
objects.desc: A whole dire-wolf pelt spread head and all before the hearth, the grey ruff bristling still. A hall grows quieter when a guest first sees it.

objects.name: Cave Bear Rug
objects.desc: An enormous cave-bear pelt, its head mounted with the jaws agape. It takes two to lay it out and it swallows half a floor.

objects.name: Sabretooth Rug
objects.desc: A tawny sabretooth hide, the great curved fangs left in the mounted skull. Few things say a colony has hunted the deep places quite so plainly.

objects.name: Claw Totem
objects.desc: A carved post hung with fans of predator claws that tick and clatter in a draught. Raised over a camp, it tells anything that comes near what lives here.

objects.name: Log Splitting Stump
objects.desc: A split log set on end as a chopping stump. With an axe, splits logs into firewood and branches.

objects.name: Timber Sawpit
objects.desc: A trestle frame with a fixed saw for ripping logs into planks. The saw needs bronze, so planks are a bronze-age unlock that opens furniture, better walls, roofs and storage.

objects.name: Potter's Kiln
objects.desc: A clay-and-stone kiln. Fires green clay into hard brick, urns, casting molds and roof tiles. Needs real heat, peat or charcoal.

objects.name: Fire-brick Kiln
objects.desc: A fire-brick kiln that holds far greater heat than a potter's kiln. Fires fine ceramics and refractory wares green-clay kilns cannot reach. Needs charcoal or coal heat.

objects.name: Granite Stonecutter's Bench
objects.desc: A heavy work slab with chisels and a dressing rail. Cuts quarried rock into clean blocks and roofing tiles.

objects.name: Bone Carver's Bench
objects.desc: A pitted worktop of antler tines and rasps, strewn with bone-dust. Splits great bones for hafts, carves tusk down to ivory, and works trophies from what a beast leaves behind.

objects.name: Ivory Idol
objects.desc: A figure carved whole from a single great tusk, pale and cold to the touch. It draws the eye and lends a hall the weight of a place that has taken great beasts and lived.

objects.name: Granite Charcoal Pit
objects.desc: An earth-covered mound where wood smoulders into charcoal over hours. The first path to metal-smelting heat, and a source of ash.

objects.name: Timber Rope Frame
objects.desc: A long covered lane of posts and a twisting hook. Strands of cordage are laid out and walked into strong rope, the kind a well windlass or rigging needs.

objects.name: Draw Well
objects.desc: A stone-lined shaft dug down to the water table, with a windlass and rope-hung bucket. Safe water with no river nearby, but a hard, costly dig, and it needs real rope for the draw.

objects.name: Cheese Basin
objects.desc: Coopered staves pitched tight, the same work as a bucket, with a straining cloth tied across the mouth. Milk goes in, the whey drains off, and what stays behind is pressed and salted until it will keep a winter.

objects.name: Smoking Rack
objects.desc: Green branches lashed into a frame over a low smouldering fire, with the food hung well above the flame. The smoke keeps the flies off and dries the flesh slowly enough that it keeps for a season. Damp wood smokes better than dry.

objects.name: Drying Rack
objects.desc: Lashed branches strung with cord for air- and smoke-drying meat and fruit. Hung here, raw meat cures into dried meat and apples, berries and grapes shrivel into dried fruit, wherever it's warm and dry, much quicker beside a fire. Holds the cured stores too. The salt-free way to keep food.

objects.name: Branch Curing Frame
objects.desc: A frame of lashed branches for stretching and curing hides with ash or salt, so they keep instead of rotting.

objects.name: Steel-Tooled Tailor's Bench
objects.desc: A long bench with a stitching horse at one end and a pattern rack at the other, laid out so a whole harness can be cut, fitted and laced without moving it. What a currier's bench does for one hide, this does for a set.

objects.name: Plank Currier's Bench
objects.desc: A staking beam and graining board for working tanned beast leather supple — oiling, stretching and slicking a stiff hide into a prime, drapeable skin.

objects.name: Soaking Trough
objects.desc: A long plank trough kept brim-full of water. Sanded hafts are weighted under and left to soak and season — a whole batch at once, needing no tending, until the grain sets hard.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Smelting Hearth
objects.desc: A fired-brick forge with bellows. Smelts copper, tin, lead and gold ores into bars and casts bronze. Needs charcoal or coal heat.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Bloomery
objects.desc: A tall iron-smelting furnace. Reduces iron ore with coal and limestone flux into iron bars, and casts steel. The hottest mundane fire.

objects.name: Iron Anvil
objects.desc: A heavy iron anvil, smithing tools and a grinding wheel. Forges metal bars into tools, weapons and armour, and grinds the edges that blades need.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Casting Hearth
objects.desc: A crucible furnace over a sand-and-clay molding floor. Melts copper and tin together and pours the bronze into clay molds, the bronze-age way to cast blades, fittings and tools. Each mold is broken to free the casting, so it is spent like any other material.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Finery Forge
objects.desc: A charcoal hearth with a forced blast that burns the carbon back out of brittle pig iron, leaving soft, tough wrought iron under the hammer. Slow and hungry for fuel, and the only way to turn a blast furnace's output into something forgeable.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Cementation Furnace
objects.desc: A sealed brick chest where bars of wrought iron are packed in charcoal and baked for days on end. The iron drinks in carbon until its skin rises in blisters.

objects.name: Fire-brick Puddling Furnace
objects.desc: A reverberatory hearth where a puddler stirs molten pig iron with a long rod, dragging the carbon out of it by hand. Brutal work, and it turns out steel by the cartload.

objects.name: Wooden Table
objects.desc: A planked table nailed together with iron. A proper surface to eat and gather at, a comfort that lifts a colony's spirits.

objects.name: Wooden Stool
objects.desc: A simple three-legged plank stool. Somewhere to sit other than the dirt.

objects.name: Larder Cupboard
objects.desc: A clay-lined plank cupboard, shelved top to bottom and kept cool and shaded. It holds more than anything else the colony can build, and the cool lining slows the turn.

objects.name: Hay Rack
objects.desc: A slatted branch frame for spreading cut grass off the wet ground to cure. Plant fibre stacked here dries into hay far faster than on the open ground, faster still beside a fire, and it holds the finished fodder too.

objects.name: Meat Hooks
objects.desc: Iron hooks on a roped rail for hanging carcasses and joints in the cool and airy. Keeps meat off the ground and slows the turn, for meat and carcasses only.

objects.name: Rope-Hung Granary
objects.desc: Grain sacks slung from ropes on a hewn staddle frame, lifted clear of the damp ground. Keeps grain and seed dry and slow to spoil, and stores nothing but grain and seed.
line: Grain / Grain Seed / Turnip Seed / Onion Seed / Bean Seed / Pea Seed / Cabbage Seed / Fibre Seed

objects.name: Root Clamp
objects.desc: A mound of roots layered in straw and earth, the old way of overwintering turnips and the like in the cool ground. Excellent keeping for root vegetables; takes nothing else.

objects.name: Thatch Roof
objects.desc: Bundled-reed roofing on a tile. Cheap shelter overhead, rots and needs re-thatching.

objects.name: Tiled Roof
objects.desc: Fired clay-tile roof. The durable, low-maintenance, storm-proof roof, visually it shades the interior but lets you see in.

objects.name: Overhead Mountain
objects.desc: Solid rock overhead, the natural roof left when a mountain is mined out. It needs the surrounding rock to hold it up; carve too wide and the unsupported span comes down.

objects.name: Plank Door
objects.desc: A hinged plank door, access through a wall while keeping a home enclosed.

objects.name: Branch Window
objects.desc: A wind-eye, a shuttered opening cut in a wall, closed with a board against the cold. Lets daylight in so pawns can work by day without torches.

objects.name: Snare
objects.desc: A noose of cord on a bent sapling. Catches small game, rabbits and rats, while you work elsewhere.

objects.name: Deadfall Trap
objects.desc: A heavy stone propped to fall on a baited trigger. Catches larger game than a snare, sometimes a boar.

objects.name: Branch Wall
objects.desc: A flimsy wall made from lashed branches. Barely slows attackers but defines a space. Rots in the weather and needs frequent repair.

objects.name: Wicker Wall
objects.desc: Woven plant-fiber wall panels. Sturdier than branch walls, good windbreak.

objects.name: Daub Wall
objects.desc: Wicker reinforced with clay daub. Solid, weather-resistant wall.

objects.name: Mud Brick Wall
objects.desc: A wall of sun-dried mud bricks. Pcordager permanent construction.

objects.name: Stone Block Wall
objects.desc: Dressed stone blocks bedded in lime mortar. A true masonry wall, dry, warm and near-permanent.

objects.name: Reinforced Concrete Wall
objects.desc: Roman concrete poured around drawn rebar. The strongest mundane wall, needs both the stone chain and the metal chain to meet.

objects.name: Runed Concrete Wall
objects.desc: Concrete kneaded with gem-dust until the runes glow in the cure. Resists blade, weather and spell, and knits its own cracks. The magic wall age.

objects.name: Branch Door
objects.desc: A simple hinged frame of lashed branches. Marks an entrance through a wall.

objects.name: Packed-Earth Floor
objects.desc: Earth tamped flat and hard underfoot. A plain dry surface that beats walking through mud, the first floor, before planks or stone.

objects.name: Plank Floor
objects.desc: Sawn planks laid over the bare ground. Quick and dry to cross, the comfortable indoor floor of a settled colony.

objects.name: Flagstone Floor
objects.desc: Cut granite flags fitted tight. The fastest, driest footing a mundane colony can lay, stays clean through any weather.

objects.name: Branch Floor
objects.desc: Branches laid corduroy over the mud and lashed down. Uneven and gappy, but it keeps boots out of the worst of the muck, the crudest floor there is.

objects.name: Rush Floor
objects.desc: Dry rushes and hay strewn thick over the ground. Soft and slow underfoot, but warm and dry, it soaks the damp up off the earth. Needs renewing as it's trodden down.

objects.name: Rammed-Clay Floor
objects.desc: Clay rammed and smoothed into a hard, even surface. Quick to cross and shrugs off ground damp, a solid floor before brick or stone.

objects.name: Mud-Brick Floor
objects.desc: Sun-dried mud bricks laid and grouted into a paved floor. Firm and dry, nearly the equal of flagstone, from clay rather than quarried rock.

objects.name: Sleeping Spot
objects.desc: A cleared patch of ground marked as a sleeping area. Better than collapsing wherever you stand.

objects.name: Hay Bed
objects.desc: A thick pile of dried hay bound with cordage, propped on branches. Proper rest. Significantly better fatigue recovery than bare ground.

objects.name: Hide Bed
objects.desc: A bed of cured hides over a hay-stuffed frame. Warmer and softer than bare hay, deeper, faster rest.

objects.name: Leather Bed
objects.desc: A planked bedstead with a stuffed leather mattress. The best rest a mundane colony can build, full, restorative sleep.

objects.name: Feather Bed
objects.desc: A bedstead under a cotton tick stuffed with a mountain of down feathers. The softest, warmest sleep there is, it eats feathers by the sackful.

objects.name: Cushioned Chair
objects.desc: A planked chair with a fat stuffed cushion. A real seat, soft enough to linger in.

objects.name: Couch
objects.desc: A long upholstered couch, three cushions deep over a planked frame. Seats the household in comfort, and swallows a heap of stuffing.

objects.name: Log Stool
objects.desc: A sawn log end on three pegged legs. Somewhere to sit off the cold ground.

objects.name: Wicker Chair
objects.desc: A chair woven from branches with a fleece-stuffed pad. Yielding enough to sit a while.

objects.name: Tacked Chair
objects.desc: A planked chair with a fleece seat held down by rows of copper tacks. The first proper joinery, sturdier than anything lashed with cord.

objects.name: Padded Bench
objects.desc: A planked bench under a thick fleece pad, long enough to stretch out on.

objects.name: Armchair
objects.desc: A deep leather-and-fleece armchair on a pegged frame. The finest seat a hall can offer, a place to sink into.

objects.name: Wool-Tick Bed
objects.desc: A planked bedstead under a tick packed with fleece. Warm, yielding rest, the proper bed before leather and down.

objects.name: Hewn Table
objects.desc: A split-log slab on trestle legs, lashed with cordage. A rough surface to eat and gather at.

objects.name: Beam Weaving Frame
objects.desc: A simple loom frame lashed from branches. Processes flax into cloth.

objects.name: Sandstone Lapidary Bench
objects.desc: A treadle wheel and a tray of wet sand. Sand will bite anything softer than itself, which is enough for moonstone, amethyst and citrine and not nearly enough for a ruby.

objects.name: Emery Grinding Bench
objects.desc: The same wheel charged with emery instead of sand. The grit is harder, so the stones that shrugged off a sand wheel — emerald, topaz — finally take an edge.

objects.name: Steel Faceting Lathe
objects.desc: A geared lathe with a steel dop and a lap charged with crushed corundum. Nothing is harder than a corundum but another corundum, which is what finally lets a ruby or a sapphire be cut rather than merely polished.

objects.name: Attunement Bench
objects.desc: A jeweller's bench of shaped stone and bronze tools. Cuts and polishes crystals into trade gems, and, once Attunement is researched, attunes mana-infused crystals and sets them into rings and amulets.

objects.name: Heartwood Runecarver's Bench
objects.desc: A carving bench of heartwood and dressed stone, its surface scored with channelling runes. Cuts a magic-wood stave and seats a polished crystal to make a first elemental staff, INT, not muscle, drives the blast. The apprentice's bench, a bloomery to the altar's finery.

objects.name: Attunement Altar
objects.desc: A marble altar ringed with gold leaf and fire-brick, where an infused crystal is bound into a staff under sustained heat. The hottest, fussiest arcane work a colony can do, the finery-forge of magic. The altar itself takes an attuned gem, so the gem chain must run first.

objects.name: Wicker Compost Bin
objects.desc: A slatted timber bin where rotten scraps and hay break down into rich compost over days. The colony's waste becomes the farm's best soil. Feed it spoiled food, hides and hay.

objects.name: Lay Poor Soil
objects.desc: Work some dirt and a little compost into barren ground to bring it to poor soil (25% fertility), enough for hardy crops.

objects.name: Lay Loam
objects.desc: Work fertiliser, compost, clay and dirt together into crumbly loam (50% fertility), good tilth for most crops.

objects.name: Lay Rich Soil
objects.desc: A heavy working of fertiliser, compost, clay and dirt builds dark, rich soil (75% fertility), the best ground that occurs in nature.

objects.name: Lay Terra Preta
objects.desc: Black earth, built by working in a fortune of fertiliser, compost, clay and dirt. The peak soil (100% fertility), only here do prize crops flourish.

objects.name: Granite Quern
objects.desc: A pair of hand millstones for grinding grain into flour. The first step from a field of wheat to a loaf of bread.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Hearth
objects.desc: A fired-brick firebox with a proper flue, so the heat goes up the chimney instead of into the room. It holds a steady fire on a fraction of the wood an open pit swallows.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Stove
objects.desc: A closed brick box with pot-holes cut through the top. The fire never touches the food, which means it can be banked low and left, and a pot can simmer all afternoon on a handful of sticks.

objects.name: Iron Stove
objects.desc: Cast plates over a brick firebox. Iron takes the heat and gives it back slowly and evenly, so nothing catches on the bottom and the fire can be smaller than the cooking.

objects.name: Steel Stove
objects.desc: A fire-brick lined range with a damper on the flue, so the draught itself is adjustable. Several pots at different heats at once, and the fuel bill of a single hearth.

objects.name: Donkey Mill
objects.desc: A pair of dressed stones on a centre post with a beam for an animal to walk. It never tires the way an arm does, and it does not stop to rest.

objects.name: Watermill
objects.desc: A breastshot wheel geared to a stone through a wooden pit-wheel. The river does the work and asks for nothing, so long as it is running.

objects.name: Windmill
objects.desc: Four cloth sails on a turning cap, geared down to a runner stone. It grinds where there is no river, which is most places.

objects.name: Stone-Vaulted Oven
objects.desc: A domed firebrick chamber with a separate flue, fired then swept out so the bread bakes on the stored heat rather than in the smoke.

objects.name: Iron-Door Oven
objects.desc: Two ovens sharing one firebox and a peel rack between them, so one is heating while the other is drawn. The heat stops being a thing you wait for.

objects.name: Steel Deck Oven
objects.desc: Fire-brick chambers behind steel doors with a damper on each flue. Every shelf can be held at a different heat, and none of them wander.

objects.name: Copper Brewing Kettle
objects.desc: A copper over its own firebox with a mash tun beside it and a cooling trough behind. Boiling the wort is what stops a batch turning, and this boils properly.

objects.name: Steel Lagering Vat
objects.desc: A stone undercroft kept cold enough that a cask can be left for months without souring. Time is the ingredient; this is what buys it.

objects.name: Runed Brewing Vat
objects.desc: A sealed still-house whose vessels hold a heat that never quite reaches the wood around them. What ferments in here keeps its edge.

objects.name: Clay-Brick Oven
objects.desc: A domed clay oven that holds an even baking heat. Turns flour and fillings into bread, pies and roasts.

objects.name: Wooden Fermenting Tun
objects.desc: A row of covered casks where malt and fruit ferment over days into ale, wine and cider. Needs a mild, steady warmth: too cold and the brew sleeps, too hot and it spoils.

objects.name: Plank Carpenter's Bench
objects.desc: A proper joiner's bench, vice, saw and nails. Built from your first saw and a batch of planks. Unlocks buckets, barrels, fine furniture, shields and bows in bulk.

objects.name: Potter's Wheel
objects.desc: A kick-wheel with a heavy stone flywheel for throwing jugs, pots and vessels, far faster and finer than coil-building by hand.

objects.name: Bronze-Spindle Spinning Wheel
objects.desc: A treadle wheel and spindle that walks flax or wool into strong thread, the binding and warp that supersedes raw cordage from the bronze age on.

objects.name: Fire-brick Porcelain Kiln
objects.desc: A clean workshop and high kiln for levigating fine white clay and firing translucent porcelain, the summit of the potter's craft.

objects.name: Fire-brick Blast Furnace
objects.desc: A tall stone stack with forced draught, smelting iron and flux to steel in bulk, the volume a finery forge cannot match.

objects.name: Fire-brick Crucible
objects.desc: Sealed clay crucibles in a coke furnace, melting iron and flux to pour homogeneous crucible steel, finer than any bloom.

objects.name: Steel Clockwork Bench
objects.desc: A precision bench of files, jigs and a hand-lathe for cutting steel gears, axles and springs into mechanisms, the heart of mills, hammers and clockwork.

objects.name: Oak Tanning Pit
objects.desc: A sunken plank-lined pit charged with tanning brine. Cured hide soaks in it for days, drinking in the tannin. Scale leather by digging more pits.

objects.name: Iron-Hooped Tanning Pit
objects.desc: A deeper pit charged with fierce beast brine, a tannin liquor strong enough to bite into thick beast hide. Ordinary brine can't touch it.

objects.name: Steeping Vat
objects.desc: A great fixed tub of plank and hoop, sunk to the rim. Brews tanning brine, bark, salt, ash-lye and water left to pickle over days. A passive timer.

objects.name: Clay Still
objects.desc: A bench of alembic, retort and glassware. Brews potions, distils dyes and tannin, renders glue and soap, the medieval-fantasy chem lab, run on herbs and gem-dust.

objects.name: Copper Still
objects.desc: A cabinet of tinctures, a fractioning still and a cold slab for handling humours. Where a plain lab boils, this draws essences off clean, the work that turns a beast's organ into a controlled draught.

objects.name: Gem-Dust Manaforge
objects.desc: An anvil ringed with glyph-light, its heat drawn from bound mana. Forges magic-alloy weapons and armour and rune-etched tools no mundane smithy can.

objects.name: Runed Crucible Furnace
objects.desc: A crucible that melts steel and gem-dust into magic-alloy bars, the feedstock of mythic metalwork.

objects.name: Ironwood Runic Loom
objects.desc: A loom strung with gem-dust thread. Weaves enchant-thread and prestige cloth shot through with bound mana.

objects.name: Heartwood Glyph Bench
objects.desc: A mason's banker fitted with gem-dust chisels. Cuts runed blocks for the magic wall age.

objects.name: Runed Still
objects.desc: An alchemy lab augmented with a mana-fed alembic. Distils high-tier potions and transmutes lesser matter to greater.

objects.name: Heartwood Joiner's Bench
objects.desc: A master joiner's bench fed with gem-dust binder. Shapes prestige and magic-wood furniture and the stocks of enchanted bows.

objects.name: Palisade
objects.desc: A wall of sharpened logs driven upright. A quick, sturdy fortification, the branch wall grown teeth.

objects.name: Barricade
objects.desc: A low heap of stakes and timber. Can't be crossed, but a defender beside it fights from cover, and can see and shoot over it.

objects.name: Gatehouse
objects.desc: A fortified stone gateway through a wall, block and mortar around a heavy timber gate. The strong point of a curtain wall.

objects.name: Plank Resin Tap
objects.desc: A spile and collecting pot that draws pitch from conifer bark and heartwood. A slow, steady source of resin, the binder the whole glue-and-bucket chain runs on.

objects.name: Grey Wolf
objects.desc: Grey shapes at the treeline, patient and pack-wise; alone one is little, but they seldom come alone. The winter pelt tans well — if you can drop it before the others close.

objects.name: Great Wolf
objects.desc: The wolf of firelit warnings, grown to the size of a pony and older than any living pack. What can be cut from such a beast is worth more than its weight in common hide — but few return to do the cutting.

objects.name: Brown Bear
objects.desc: Slow to rouse and terrible once roused; the thick hide turns a careless blow, though the belly does not. A single one yields hide and meat enough to keep a household a season.

objects.name: Goblin Raider
objects.desc: Runty and vicious, it fights with whatever cruel little blade it has scavenged, edged with something that stings long after the cut. Kill enough and their nasty gear is yours — weak as it is.

objects.name: Plague Rat
objects.desc: Bloated on middens and bold only in the swarm, it scatters the moment the numbers turn. Even the cook-pot takes it grudgingly, and only once the stores run thin.

objects.name: Grave Shade
objects.desc: A knot of cold that drifts through solid rock and leaves frost where it lingers; steel bites it poorly, but living flame makes it flinch. It falls fast once struck, and leaves nothing behind but the chill.

objects.name: Red Deer
objects.desc: It grazes with its head forever coming up, gone at a snapped twig — the keen-eyed ones are hard to stalk. Clean venison and a soft hide reward the patient.

objects.name: Cottontail
objects.desc: A nervous scrap of fur that lives one bound from its burrow, gone down the hole at a passing shadow. A quiet snare puts one in the evening stew before it ever knows the hand was there.

objects.name: Wild Boar
objects.desc: A slab of muscle on trotters that answers a wound with a charge, tusks first. Dangerous to corner, but the meat is rich and the hide stubborn enough to be worth the curing.

objects.name: Woodland Elk
objects.desc: Broad through the shoulder and crowned in antler, it would sooner flee than fight — until the flight is cut off. Meat, hide and bone in plenty, and the calm-handed sometimes break one to the saddle.

objects.name: Bighorn
objects.desc: It picks along ledges that would kill a wolf, cropping what little grows up there. Easily kept for its milk, once you catch one off the rocks.

objects.name: Junglefowl
objects.desc: A flighty bird that scratches the dirt and lays where it wanders, forever startled by its own shadow. A coop keeps it laying; a lean week ends it in the pot.

objects.name: Wild Ox
objects.desc: The great wild ox the old herders never quite tamed; it ignores you until it doesn't, and then a ton of horn and muscle is on you. One carcass feeds a camp — one broken to the yoke changes a season.

objects.name: Grey Tusker
objects.desc: A walking relic of the ice-times, its shaggy hide shrugging off frost and near everything else — only fire troubles it. Bring one down and there is ivory, meat and hide for a whole holdfast, if a whole warband survives the trying.

objects.name: Grey Hippogriff
objects.desc: Eagle to the fore and horse behind, it watches from the crags and stoops faster than a loosed arrow. Prized alive as a mount by those bold enough to gentle it; prized dead for feathers and hide by those who cannot.

objects.name: Snow Hoarfowl
objects.desc: A plump frost-feathered fowl of the cold north, untroubled by winter and wary only of the cook-fire. Kept for its eggs, taken for its down.

objects.name: Barbed Quillback
objects.desc: A shuffling fortress of quills that only the reckless grapple; the wise go for the soft underside. Its spines are worth the harvesting, once you find the way past them.

objects.name: Grey Worg
objects.desc: Blacker and broader than any honest wolf, it hunts men from choice rather than hunger — and hunts them well by dark. The pelt is fine and deep, reason enough to hunt it back.

objects.name: Golden Jackal
objects.desc: It yips in the dark and grows brave in numbers, snatching what stronger killers leave. Quick and slight, it rarely stands to fight — and rarely leaves more than a thin, dust-coloured hide.

objects.name: Tawny Owlbear
objects.desc: A thing that should not be — a bear's fury behind an owl's flat, staring hate — and it charges on sight. Its coarse hide and cruel beak fetch a grim price, and the maddest few even try to raise one.

objects.name: Sabretooth Cat
objects.desc: A great cat built around a single killing bite; it commits to one lunge and rarely needs a second. Fast and sharp-eyed, hard to catch flat-footed — but the striped hide is a trophy worth the risk.

objects.name: Bog Lurker
objects.desc: A drifting log in the reeds until the water erupts and the jaws close; its plated back turns steel, its belly far less so. Sluggish in the cold, and its thick hide makes leather worth the wading.

objects.name: Fen Adder
objects.desc: A green ribbon in the reeds whose bite is small and whose venom is not — the wound outlasts the walk home. Slight and cold-slowed; kill it for safety more than gain.

objects.name: Fen Stirge
objects.desc: A ragged-winged bloodsucker that gorges and drops away swollen; one is a nuisance, a swarm a slow bleeding. Struck down it bursts to a red smear, leaving only the quiet after.

objects.name: Bog Ooze
objects.desc: A crawling knot of bog-rot and ill will that keeps moving well past when it ought to stop. Cut it down and it slumps back into the muck it rose from, taking its trouble with it.

objects.name: Cave Salamander
objects.desc: Blind and pale in the lightless pools, it has never once wanted the sun. Sluggish and harmless; the soft flesh is edible, if you can stomach a thing so wan.

objects.name: Bramble Weaver
objects.desc: It strings the barbed thickets with snare-silk and waits, hard-shelled above and venom-fanged below. The silk and the venom-glands both fetch coin from those who know their use.

objects.name: Cave Kobold
objects.desc: A small, skulking thief that fights with trap and stolen knife and bolts the instant the odds sour. Whatever it has filched off better warriors comes loose with the corpse.

objects.name: Pack Gnoll
objects.desc: A hyena that walks upright and laughs as it comes, hungry for anything weaker than itself. It swings a looted bone cleaver — crude, but yours if you leave it standing over its corpse.

objects.name: Orc Reaver
objects.desc: Broad, scarred and heedless of pain, it swings iron too heavy for most men to lift — and only a strong hand turns that iron back on its kin. Kill one and the warband only grows angrier.

objects.name: Screamer
objects.desc: A woman's shriek from a carrion-bird's throat, dropping talon-first out of the sun's glare. Cunning enough to mob a lone traveller, brittle enough to fall to one good shot.

objects.name: Bog Croaker
objects.desc: Frog-folk of the reed-beds, croaking their war-songs in a chorus meant to unnerve before the spears come. Simple and swamp-bound — dangerous in a mob, wretched alone.

objects.name: Wolf Pup
objects.desc: All ears and clumsy paws, it tumbles after the pack with more hunger than harm. Raise a blade to it and its yelping brings the grown ones back at a dead run.

objects.name: Scrawny Wolf
objects.desc: A hard winter's runt, ribs plain under a dull coat, dangerous only when there is no room left to run. The pelt is thin, but a pelt is a pelt.

objects.name: Grey Yearling
objects.desc: Past its first winter and still learning its place at the kill, bold beyond its strength. It will trade blows a wiser wolf would not, and leaves a serviceable hide.

objects.name: Timber Wolf
objects.desc: Deep-chested and thick-furred, the dependable killer at the heart of the pack. Neither swift nor armoured, but it endures — and the winter coat tans into something fine.

objects.name: Moor Runner
objects.desc: Bred long and light for the open moor, it runs its quarry down over the miles and strikes hard when it closes — with little left to soak a blow in return.

objects.name: Pack Alpha
objects.desc: The wolf the others give way to, first to the throat and quickest to the kill. Put it down swiftly, for it hits far harder than it can take — and its hide is the pack's finest.

objects.name: Scarred Hunter
objects.desc: Old wounds map every fight it has survived, and it fights like a beast with nothing left to lose. Swift and savage, no tougher for the scars — a worthy pelt for a hard kill.

objects.name: Dire Wolf
objects.desc: A wolf out of the deep-wood's memory, tall as a man's chest and faster than its size has any right to be. It deals a great deal of hurt and takes little; the great dark pelt is prize enough.

objects.name: Bloodmoon Alpha
objects.desc: They say it runs hardest under a red moon, and the whole pack runs mad behind it. A whirl of fang that must be dropped fast, before it opens the whole hunting party.

objects.name: Direwolf Matriarch
objects.desc: Grey-muzzled and merciless, she has led the pack through more winters than most men see. Neither swift nor soft any longer — a slow, sure, hard-hided fight, and a matriarch's pelt to show for it.

objects.name: Frost-Fang
objects.desc: Its breath smokes and its coat rimes white; the deep cold is kin to it, and only fire tells. Quick and cutting but thin-skinned — and the frosted pelt keeps a strange chill long after.

objects.name: Bear Cub
objects.desc: Round, clumsy and endlessly curious — and never once out of its mother's reckoning. Small game at a large risk: the sow is always nearer than she looks.

objects.name: Yearling Bear
objects.desc: Newly turned out to fend for itself and still unsure what it may take. Manageable for a careful hunter, with hide and meat enough to be worth the stalk.

objects.name: Sun Bear
objects.desc: Small for a bear, marked with a pale throat-blaze and a weakness for honey and grubs. The armoured back turns a spear where the soft belly will not.

objects.name: Black Bear
objects.desc: Shy of open ground and quicker to climb than to stand — until standing is all that's left. A thick pelt and a season's meat reward the hunter who forces the matter.

objects.name: Grizzly
objects.desc: It fears nothing afoot and turns from nothing that charges; the hide sheds glancing blows, the belly does not. One brings down meat, fat and a hide worth a whole winter's warmth.

objects.name: Cave Bear
objects.desc: A giant out of the deep caves, its jaws remembered in the gnawed bones of its own dead. Thickly hided and hard to fell — but a single carcass keeps a hall in meat and fur.

objects.name: Scarred Grizzly
objects.desc: Every winter has taken something from it and given back only spite. A heavy, plodding, punishing fight — and the battered hide is all the tougher for the scars.

objects.name: Ridgeback
objects.desc: A stiff ridge of hair runs down a back plated thick as old bark, and little short of a spear-thrust reaches through it. Slow to bleed and slower to fall — the hide alone is armour half-made.

objects.name: Elder Cave Bear
objects.desc: Ancient and enormous, it has outlasted whole tribes that dared to hunt it. To fell one is a saga in itself, and its vast hide and ivory claws the proof of the telling.

objects.name: Ironhide Bruin
objects.desc: Its hide has turned so many spears that the scars have hardened into armour of their own. Blows glance and slide; you will not out-batter it, only outlast it — and the hide is worth every hour.

objects.name: Bloodclaw
objects.desc: It kills long past its hunger, and the caked red never quite leaves its claws. Wound it and it only worsens; drop it clean, or not at all — the claws alone are a grim trophy.

objects.name: Great Bear
objects.desc: The bear the old songs raised to frighten children — a moving mountain of muscle and ancient wrath. What it leaves behind is more than meat and fur; such a beast carries something rarer in its bones.

objects.name: Piglet
objects.desc: Striped and squealing, it keeps hard to the sow's flank and bolts at a footfall. Barely a meal — and the sow will make you pay for it.

objects.name: Scrub Boar
objects.desc: Lean and low, forever rooting the scrub for whatever a snout turns up. It would sooner crash off into the brush than fight, and falls into honest meat for a ready spear.

objects.name: Young Tusker
objects.desc: Its tusks are freshly through and it is far too eager to try them, all squeal and no weight behind the swing. A clean kill for a steady spear, and hide enough to cure.

objects.name: Razorback
objects.desc: A ridge of bristle stands along its spine when the temper rises, and it rises at nothing. It comes fast when it comes; the hide is coarse but stubborn, worth the curing.

objects.name: Bristleback
objects.desc: Broad through the shoulder and matted in hide and gristle thick enough to blunt a spear. It soaks more than it deals, and gives back good leather for the effort.

objects.name: Elder Tusker
objects.desc: Old, solitary and long past patience, its tusks worn to yellow scythes. A stubborn kill — but the ivory and the heavy hide reward a hunter who stands their ground.

objects.name: Irontusk
objects.desc: Tusks like ploughshares and a hide that stopped answering to fear seasons ago. Hard to wound and harder to turn, but there is fine ivory in that ugly head.

objects.name: Grey Sow-Mother
objects.desc: She herds a squealing brood, and there is nothing in the wood she will not gore to keep it. Slow to fell and quick to anger — a thick hide and a great deal of meat for the patient.

objects.name: Direboar
objects.desc: A boar the size of a bullock that charges the way an avalanche falls, trampling what its tusks miss. It costs blood to bring down and repays it in ivory, hide and meat.

objects.name: Blackmane Tusker
objects.desc: A black crest bristling to the shoulder, fast for its bulk and faster still to rage. It hits like a landslide but bleeds freely — end it quickly, and the great tusks are yours.

objects.name: Bog Colossus
objects.desc: It wallows the deep mire caked in dried mud thick as a shield, huge and slow and hard to stop. Wading it down is grim work, rewarded with hide and tusk enough to justify it.

objects.name: Great Boar
objects.desc: The tusker of hunters' boasts and hunters' nightmares, that fells saplings where it merely turns. Few beasts yield so grand a trophy — to the fewer still standing when it falls.

objects.name: Goblin Sneak
objects.desc: It would sooner sink a blade in a back than face a front, and usually contrives to. Its scavenged gear is mean and poison-smeared, but it comes free with the corpse.

objects.name: Goblin Whelp
objects.desc: Barely off the carrion pile, it flings itself into the fray to prove teeth it has not yet grown. One is nothing; they are never one, and the swarm carries a weight the whelp cannot.

objects.name: Cave Goblin
objects.desc: Pale and saucer-eyed from a life under stone, it flinches at daylight and little else. Fleet in the dark, it is gone with its stolen scraps before a slow hand can close the gap.

objects.name: Goblin Cutter
objects.desc: It has learned exactly which way a knife goes in and takes an ugly pride in the knowing. A steadier hand than most of its kin — and a nastier little blade to strip from it.

objects.name: Goblin Netter
objects.desc: It fights with weighted net and hooked stick and likes its prey tangled before it strikes. Ungovernable in a pack; the net alone is a curiosity worth lifting.

objects.name: Goblin Bloodrager
objects.desc: Work it into a froth and it forgets, for a while, that it is a coward. Frenzy makes it brave, not strong — cut it down before the froth peaks.

objects.name: Goblin Slinker
objects.desc: Quick, low and greased with river-mud, gone from where the blade falls before it lands. It stings and slips away; corner it, for it cannot take what it dishes out.

objects.name: Goblin Boss
objects.desc: It rules its warren by being meaner than the next goblin, and no cleverer. Kill it and the warren squabbles — and its hoarded gear falls to the victor.

objects.name: Goblin Warchief
objects.desc: It clawed to the top of the heap and dares the pack to test the claim. Sharper and deadlier than the rabble it drives, with the best of their scavenged iron on its own belt.

objects.name: Hobgoblin Champion
objects.desc: Taller and better-drilled than the rabble it leads, and insufferably aware of it. It fights with a discipline the others lack — and carries gear actually worth the taking.

objects.name: Goblin Firecaller
objects.desc: It hoards fire-pots and burning tricks and cackles at every flame it sets. Deadly at a distance and useless up close — close the gap fast, before the whole warren is alight.

objects.name: Goblin Warlord
objects.desc: Cunning enough to bind a hundred squabbling goblins to a single purpose, usually your undoing. The best gear of the whole warband hangs off its frame, and it did not gather that by being weak.

objects.name: Orc Whelp
objects.desc: Young and untried, all snarl and no scars, hungry to earn its first. Strong for its age already; the crude iron it carries wants a strong arm to swing in turn.

objects.name: Orc Grunt
objects.desc: The plain bulk of any warband — strong, blunt and wholly without doubt. Its heavy iron is honest loot, though only a stout arm turns it to use.

objects.name: Orc Scavenger
objects.desc: It picks the field after the fighting for whatever an iron boot has left behind. Weaker than its kin and more poorly armed, but a corpse that hides fewer surprises.

objects.name: Orc Marauder
objects.desc: It raids for the sheer joy of it and counts a burned steading a fine day's work. Strong and mean, with weighty iron worth taking — if you have the shoulders to lift it.

objects.name: Orc Berserker
objects.desc: It works itself past pain and past sense and comes on regardless of its wounds. Frenzy makes it relentless, not durable — weather the storm and it falls like any other.

objects.name: Orc Veteran
objects.desc: Notched blade, notched tusks — it has buried better fighters than the one before it now. Its gear is well-used and well-kept, a proper prize for a proper fight.

objects.name: Orc Ironhide
objects.desc: Hide boiled to a leather thickness that shrugs the first blow and the second alike. A grinding kill — but that same hide, and its heavy iron, are worth the grind.

objects.name: Orc Slayer
objects.desc: It fights in a whirl of iron and means to be surrounded, the better to reach everyone at once. Keep it single and keep it moving; its blades are a fine prize once it stills.

objects.name: Orc Warlord
objects.desc: It leads from the front of every charge because nothing has yet stopped it there. Cut down, it leaves fine war-gear — and a leaderless host suddenly unsure of itself.

objects.name: Orc Blackguard
objects.desc: Sworn to its warboss and to the killing, in that order and no other. Disciplined, well-armed, and worth the danger of stripping once it is down.

objects.name: Orc Chosen
objects.desc: Marked by scar and rite as the one the tribe throws at its worst problems. Thick-hided and heavily geared — bringing one down cracks open the warlord's own hoard.

objects.name: Orc Warboss
objects.desc: It holds the whole warband by the throat of its own strength and points that strength wherever it pleases. The finest iron of the host is its own, and only the strongest hand will ever swing it back.

objects.name: Spiderling
objects.desc: A scatter of them across the web, each no larger than a thumbnail and just as sharp. Singly nothing; by the dozen, a creeping tide of little fangs.

objects.name: Web-Scuttler
objects.desc: It races the strands to whatever has blundered in, quicker than a dropped stone. Small and swift — a nip, not a wound — and a thread of usable silk.

objects.name: Thorn Hatchling
objects.desc: Small and venom-quick, its bite running colder than a thing that size has any right to. Brittle enough to crush underfoot, if you reach it before the fangs reach you.

objects.name: Ambush Weaver
objects.desc: It strings a trip-line snare and holds still as bark until the thread twitches. Armoured above and venomed below; the silk it spins is worth more than the fight.

objects.name: Bristle Spider
objects.desc: Stiff hairs bristle from a swollen body, and it holds its ground where lesser kin bolt. Hard-shelled and stubborn — its venom-glands fetch a fair price from those who dare draw them.

objects.name: Broodmother
objects.desc: She squats over a bulging egg-sac and answers every shadow with fang and flung silk. A heavier kill than her brood, and a richer one — silk, venom and all.

objects.name: Venomfang Stalker
objects.desc: It does not spin — it hunts, and its bite is a great deal worse than any snare. Swift, deadly and thin-shelled; strike first, or the venom strikes for it.

objects.name: Carapace Lurker
objects.desc: Plated dark and low to the ground, it lets blows glance off and closes at its own unhurried pace. A patient, grinding kill — and a carapace worth the salvaging.

objects.name: Great Weaver
objects.desc: It has webbed a whole hollow in silk and killed everything else that ever lived there. A formidable thing, but its lair hangs heavy with silk, and its glands heavier still with venom.

objects.name: Dread Broodmother
objects.desc: Ancient and swollen, she has seeded the wood with a hundred hungry broods. End her and you end them all — and lay claim to silk no ordinary weaver spins.

objects.name: Chitin Horror
objects.desc: So thickly armoured it scarcely reads as a spider — more a walking shield that happens to have fangs. Little will pierce it; only patience and a heavy arm bring the chitin down.

objects.name: Spider Queen
objects.desc: The heart of the web-choked dark, to whom everything that skitters answers. What can be drawn from such a matriarch is no common venom — and few hollows are darker or deadlier to enter.

objects.name: Dire Rat
objects.desc: Grown to the size of a hound on rich filth, and long past bolting from a raised stick. It holds its ground behind a mouthful of teeth, and its coarse hide will at least turn a draught.

objects.name: Greater Wraith
objects.desc: An older, colder hunger than the common wraith; the chill of it fills a room before it does. Steel slides through it, flame makes it recoil — and it leaves not even a bone behind.

objects.name: Fawn
objects.desc: Dapple-coated and wobble-legged, it freezes where its mother left it and trusts to stillness. A small, sad kill — and the doe is rarely far.

objects.name: Rabbit Kit
objects.desc: Blind-new and no bigger than a fist, it scarcely knows yet to be afraid. It fits whole in one hand, bones and all — a single mouthful for the truly desperate.

objects.name: Great Elk
objects.desc: A stag out of the old ballads, its antler-spread wider than a tall man stands. It would flee if it could and gore you through if it cannot; the crowned skull alone is a hall-worthy trophy.

objects.name: Goat Kid
objects.desc: It skitters the high ledges after its dam, sure-footed before it is sure of anything. Easily kept for the milk to come — if you can lay hands on it at all.

objects.name: Chick
objects.desc: A ball of down on toothpick legs, peeping after whatever moves and tripping over its own feet. Give it a season and it lays; take it now and there is barely a bite on it.

objects.name: Elder Aurochs
objects.desc: Grey about the muzzle and vast through the shoulder, the herd-bull no wolf tests twice. It suffers no challenge lightly — but one carcass feeds a camp, and one gentled ox works a season.

objects.name: Bull Mammoth
objects.desc: The great tusker of the herd, so vast the plain seems to tilt as it wheels; frost is nothing to it, and little else is much more. Fell one and there is ivory, hide and meat for a holdfast — should a warband survive the felling.

objects.name: Royal Hippogriff
objects.desc: A prince of the crag-winds in bright plumage, its stoop swift as a loosed arrow and its temper princely too. Coveted alive by those who would ride the sky, dead for feathers finer than any common bird's.

objects.name: Hoarfowl Chick
objects.desc: A puff of frost-white down that hasn't yet learned to fear the cold it was born to. Harmless and slight — an egg-layer in time, if a fox doesn't find it first.

objects.name: Elder Quillback
objects.desc: Grown huge and slow behind a fortress of quills that nothing sensible cares to test. A long, patient kill by way of the soft underside — and a harvest of spines for the trouble.

objects.name: Alpha Worg
objects.desc: The worg the others circle, blacker and crueller than any of them, and it hunts men for the pleasure of it. Bring it down and the pack scatters — and its dark pelt is the finest of the lot.

objects.name: Jackal Pup
objects.desc: Yipping and underfoot, it learns to scavenge long before it learns to hunt, and runs at the first raised hand. Its dying only thins a hungry pack by a single mouth.

objects.name: Elder Owlbear
objects.desc: Grizzled and enormous, its unnatural hate given a lifetime to deepen. A brutal, heavy fight — but the great beak and coarse hide make a rare and grisly prize.

objects.name: Dire Sabretooth
objects.desc: A great cat the size of a warhorse, its fangs the length of a man's forearm and its lunge a killing thing in itself. Fast, fanged and hard to weather — and its striped hide a trophy few can boast.

objects.name: Elder Crocodile
objects.desc: Moss-backed and log-still, it has taken game from this bank longer than the village has stood. Its plated hide turns near everything but a thrust to the soft belly, and makes leather worth the wading.

objects.name: Giant Viper
objects.desc: Thick as a strong man's arm and swift as a cracked whip; there is no simply walking off this one's venom. Cold-blooded and sluggish in the chill — the safest hour to take its prized skin.

objects.name: Stirgeling
objects.desc: A newly-fledged blood-drinker, all appetite and no weight, that a walking-stick swats from the air. Its ending buys nothing but one fewer bite come nightfall.

objects.name: Grime Horror
objects.desc: A wallowing mound of bog-rot and malice that seals its own wounds as fast as they open. Patience beats it where blades will not; when it finally sags, it leaves the marsh a little cleaner and nothing else.

objects.name: Elder Olm
objects.desc: Old past guessing in the lightless pools, pale as a drowned thing and just as blind. It neither flees nor fights with much conviction; the wan flesh feeds those unbothered by the look of it.

objects.name: Kobold Trapper
objects.desc: It seeds the ground with snares and deadfalls and lets the trap do its killing for it. Watch your footing more than its blade; the scraps it hoards are humble, but yours once it's dead.

objects.name: Gnoll Reaver
objects.desc: Bigger, bloodier and hungrier than the pack it runs at the head of, and laughing all the while. Its looted cleaver is heavy and cruel — a fitting reward for a hard fight.

objects.name: Harpy Matron
objects.desc: She leads the roost's stooping, shrieking mob and screams the loudest of them all. Kill her and the flock loses its nerve — and her plumage is a strange, coveted prize.

objects.name: Bullywug Brute
objects.desc: Bloated and broad, it throngs the reeds bellowing war in a chorus of croaks. Simple and swamp-bound, but heavy enough that a mob of them is no laughing matter.

objects.name: Trader
objects.desc: Road-dust on fine cloth and a ledger where a sword would hang. Every price in the county lives behind those eyes.

objects.name: Caravan Guard
objects.desc: Paid by the mile and armed by the crown, it watches the treeline the whole way through, a wall that walks beside the wares.

objects.name: Visitor
objects.desc: Come to see the colony with their own eyes, and to be seen. Word of the welcome they get travels home ahead of them.

objects.name: Pack Ox
objects.desc: A broad-backed ox that has carried half a kingdom's wares over every pass worth naming. It plods, it chews, it minds its own burden.

objects.name: Mountain-born
objects.desc: The High Crags And Deep Mountain Halls. Carved, The Old Songs Say, From The Living Roots Of The Mountains.

homelands: the high crags and deep mountain halls
wind-scoured peaks above the cloud line

objects.name: Forest-kin
objects.desc: The Deep Evergreen Forests. Born Of Seed And Shadow Beneath The First Great Canopy.

objects.name: Deep-dwellers
objects.desc: Lightless Caverns And Tunnel-Cities. Delved Up From The Roots Of The World And Never Wholly Leaving Them.

homelands: the cold dark beneath the hills

objects.name: Sky-touched
objects.desc: High Windswept Plateaus And Observatory-Towers. Said To Have Fallen, Long Ago, As Light From A Dying Star.

homelands: the thin air of the upper ranges

objects.name: Marsh-folk
objects.desc: Fetid Marshes And Flooded Lowlands. Risen, Mud-Slick And Blinking, From The First Warm Swamp.

objects.name: Tundra-clans
objects.desc: Frozen Tundra And Glacier-Fields. Bred In The Long Winter, Where Only The Unyielding Endured.

homelands: the endless white of the far north

objects.name: Ember-kin
objects.desc: Volcanic Slopes And Forge-Cities. Forged, The Smiths Say, In The Heart Of A Mountain'S Fire.

homelands: the smoking calderas of the deep south

objects.name: River-people
objects.desc: Fertile River Valleys And Trade-Deltas. Born Where The Great Rivers Braid, And Never Far From Running Water Since.

homelands: the broad slow rivers of the heartland

objects.name: Wastrel-nomads
objects.desc: Scorched Badlands And Shifting Dunes. Weathered Into Being By A Sun That Never Relents.

homelands: the trackless desert and dry steppe

objects.name: Verdant
objects.desc: Sun-Drenched Orchards And Terraced Gardens. Grown, Not Birthed, From The First Flowering Of A Kinder Age.

homelands: warm fertile lowlands thick with growth

objects.name: Wild Berries
objects.desc: Foraged berries. Small, tart, a handful barely dents real hunger.

objects.name: Carp
objects.desc: Freshwater fish. Bony but nutritious.

objects.name: Wild Oats
objects.desc: Raw gathered grain, gritty and hard on the gut eaten as-is. Mill it to flour and bake it for a proper, filling loaf.

objects.name: Wild Sage
objects.desc: Grey-green sage cropped from sunny banks. Bundled into the pot for flavour; the smoke keeps the flies off a curing hide.

objects.name: Styptic Pack
objects.desc: Powdered oak-gall and ash rammed into a wad of lint. Slammed onto a spurting wound it stops the blood at once, and it grinds filth into the flesh doing it. For the moment when a colonist is about to bleed out and there is no time to be clean.

objects.name: Wooden Arm Splint
objects.desc: Two shaved battens laid either side of the arm over a wad of linen, strapped from wrist to elbow. It holds the bone where it was set and lets the arm do nothing else at all.

objects.name: Wooden Leg Splint
objects.desc: Long battens run from thigh to ankle and lashed tight over padding. Walking on it is out of the question, which is rather the point.

objects.name: Lime Arm Cast
objects.desc: Linen soaked in slaked lime and wound around the arm, moulded to every knuckle before it goes off hard. It sets to stone overnight, and it breaks like stone too.

objects.name: Lime Leg Cast
objects.desc: A limed shell packed from thigh to toes and left to harden around the leg. Nothing shifts inside it, and nothing much shifts outside it either.

objects.name: Bone-Meal Draught
objects.desc: Ground bone stirred into spirit and bitter root, drunk down in one and kept down with difficulty. A break knits over the day that follows, and the day that follows is not one anybody would choose to be awake for.

objects.name: Emberbloom Draught
objects.desc: The coal-red flower drawn off in spirit until the liquor glows faintly. Whatever is broken is whole again before the phial is set down, and the drinker feels nothing but warmth.

objects.name: Fever Draught
objects.desc: Willow bark and sage boiled down hard and drunk scalding. It breaks a fever and drives back the heat rising off a wound that has begun to turn.

objects.name: Charcoal Purge
objects.desc: Burnt willow ground to black powder and stirred into water. It goes down foul and brings the poison back up with it, and a good deal else besides, and leaves the drinker green and wrung out for the rest of the day.

objects.name: Burn Dressing
objects.desc: Tallow and honey worked cool into a linen wrap. Laid over a burn it keeps the air off and the dressing from taking the skin with it when it comes away.

objects.name: Warming Liniment
objects.desc: Rendered fat cut with spirit and mustard seed, rubbed hard into a limb that has gone white and waxy. Brings the blood back where it has stopped going.

objects.name: Poppy Draught
objects.desc: The milk of the seed-head, thinned in spirit and measured out by drops. It takes the pain away entirely, and takes some of the patient with it for a while.

objects.name: Field Surgeon's Kit
objects.desc: Needle, curved probe, boiled thread and a folded roll of dressing, carried by someone who has done this before. It answers most of what a battle does to a body, and none of it well as the thing made for the job.

objects.name: Honey Salve
objects.desc: Woundwort worked into honey and spread on a strip of linen. Honey keeps a dressing from turning foul, which is why it was packed onto wounds for as long as anyone kept bees.

objects.name: Spirit Tincture
objects.desc: Staunchweed and sage steeped in distilled spirit until the liquor takes their colour. It bites going on and the wound stays clean, which nobody could explain and everybody noticed.

objects.name: Surgeon's Dressing
objects.desc: Boiled linen, a measure of tincture and a splint of thin steel, rolled together and kept sealed until it is wanted. The first dressing that assumes someone knows what they are doing.

objects.name: Emberbloom Balm
objects.desc: The coal-red flower rendered down with tallow and bound with gem-dust. It goes on cold and the flesh under it runs hot for a day afterwards, closing over faster than it has any business doing.

objects.name: Woundwort
objects.desc: Bitter staunchweed pulled from the ditches. The old folk pack it onto a gash to slow the bleeding, chew it raw in a pinch.

objects.name: Chewed Poultice
objects.desc: Woundwort mashed between the teeth to a green spit-paste and lashed over the wound with cord. Crude, foul, but it works.

objects.name: River Trout
objects.desc: A prized freshwater fish. Rich and delicate.

objects.name: Rabbit Carcass
objects.desc: Freshly hunted rabbit. Process it to get meat.

objects.name: Deer Carcass
objects.desc: A large game animal. Process for venison and hide.

objects.name: Rabbit Meat
objects.desc: Lean rabbit meat, ready to cook.

objects.name: Venison
objects.desc: Rich deer meat. Filling and nutritious.

objects.name: Rotten Hide
objects.desc: A hide left too long, slimy and useless. Scrap.

objects.name: Coney Fur
objects.desc: Downy rabbit fur. Warm out of all proportion to its weight, and about as tough as wet paper.

objects.name: Vermin Hide
objects.desc: Patchy rat skin. Thin and quick to split, but it costs almost nothing.

objects.name: Buckskin
objects.desc: Supple deerskin. Takes a soft drape that suits shirts and light bags.

objects.name: Kidskin
objects.desc: Fine goat leather. Soft enough for gloves and close-fitting garments.

objects.name: Jackal Leather
objects.desc: Thin desert-jackal hide. Light and shrugs off dry heat, though it wears through quickly.

objects.name: Wolf Leather
objects.desc: Tough wolf leather with a warm nap. Holds up to hard wear in the cold.

objects.name: Worg Leather
objects.desc: Dense worg hide, heavier and warmer than a common wolf's.

objects.name: Boarhide
objects.desc: Stiff, bristled boar hide, thickest across the shoulders. It comes out of the tanning bucket hard enough to back a shield without complaint.

objects.name: Elk Leather
objects.desc: Broad elk leather, tough yet still pliable. A dependable all-round armour skin.

objects.name: Oxhide
objects.desc: Rigid aurochs hide, thick as a plank. Stiffens into heavy plates, straps, and shield facings.

objects.name: Bearhide
objects.desc: Deep, shaggy bear leather. Heavy on the shoulders and blessedly warm.

objects.name: Cave Bear Hide
objects.desc: Immense cave-bear hide, the thickest a hunter is likely to bring home. Weighs like armour on its own.

objects.name: Owlbear Leather
objects.desc: Coarse owlbear hide, oddly tough and strange to the touch.

objects.name: Sabretooth Leather
objects.desc: Sabretooth pelt with a dense, handsome fur. A skin worn to be seen.

objects.name: Mammoth Leather
objects.desc: Vast mammoth hide under a wool coat. Ponderous to work and warm enough for the deep cold.

objects.name: Hippogriff Leather
objects.desc: Light, feather-flecked hippogriff hide. Airy to wear and prized for its sheen.

objects.name: Direwolf Leather
objects.desc: Prime direwolf pelt, warm and striking. The mark of a serious hunter.

objects.desc: Ash- or salt-cured rabbit skin. Stable and slow to rot, ready for the tanning bucket.
