objects.name: Spit-Roasted Meat
objects.desc: Meat skewered on a branch and cooked over fire. Simple, filling.

objects.name: Stew
objects.desc: A thin stew of two cuts boiled in the pot. Plain but filling. Requires a clay cooking pot.

objects.name: Fine Stew
objects.desc: A proper stew of three cuts, simmered thick and hearty. Requires a clay cooking pot.

objects.name: Lavish Stew
objects.desc: A rich feast-stew of four cuts, dense with meat and marrow. A pot to be proud of. Requires a clay cooking pot.

objects.name: Pottage
objects.desc: A thick boiled mess of garden vegetables. Peasant fare, but it warms and fills.

objects.name: Branch
objects.desc: A dry woody branch. Burns quickly and lashes together easily. Used in nearly everything early on.

objects.name: Small Stone
objects.desc: A small, loose stone. Useful for crafting.

objects.name: Flint Shard
objects.desc: A knapped flint chip. Sharp edge, primitive cutting tool blank.

objects.name: Plant Fiber
objects.desc: Stripped plant stalks. Twisted into rope, woven into walls, or dried into hay.

objects.name: Bark
objects.desc: Peeled tree bark. Burns slowly and steadily.

objects.name: Hay
objects.desc: Dried grass stalks. Soft bedding material, thatching, or animal fodder.

objects.name: Pine Log
objects.desc: Softwood log. Cheap bulk construction and the common firewood; the workhorse timber.

objects.name: Birch Log
objects.desc: Light utility timber; the best firewood and bark-rich for tanning.

objects.name: Apple Log
objects.desc: Dense, close-grained fruitwood from a felled apple tree. Fine carving stock and a slow, fragrant firewood.

objects.name: Oak Log
objects.desc: Dense hardwood. Furniture, heavy beams, durable construction.

objects.name: Ash Log
objects.desc: Tough, springy timber. Tool hafts, polearms, and shields.

objects.name: Willow Log
objects.desc: Light, soft riverbank timber. Easy to work but weak, wicker, fuel, and rough boards.

objects.name: Yew Log
objects.desc: Premium, rare timber. Bows and fine furniture.

objects.name: Green Firewood
objects.desc: Freshly split wood, still damp. Burns poorly and smokes. Season it near a fire to dry.

objects.name: Dry Firewood
objects.desc: Seasoned firewood. The best wood fuel, hot and clean for hearth and campfire.

objects.name: Sawdust
objects.desc: Fine wood dust from sawing. Tinder, smoking fuel, and later a binder.

objects.name: Peat
objects.desc: Cut turf from a bog. Cheap, smoky mid-heat fuel; dry it like firewood before burning.

objects.name: Charcoal
objects.desc: Wood charred low and slow in a pit. Clean, high heat, the first fuel hot enough to smelt metal.

objects.name: Coal
objects.desc: Mined coal. A hot, efficient fuel that smelts iron, but its sulphur spoils steel, so it must first be baked into coke.

objects.name: Coke
objects.desc: Coal baked airless in an oven until the sulphur and tar burn off, leaving near-pure carbon. The fiercest mundane fire there is, the only fuel that will make steel.

objects.name: Malachite
objects.desc: Green copper carbonate ore. The common, easily-smelted copper ore.

objects.name: Chalcopyrite
objects.desc: Brassy copper-iron sulphide. Rich copper ore, more bar per smelt.

objects.name: Azurite
objects.desc: Deep-blue copper ore. Lean but pretty; also a pigment.

objects.name: Cassiterite
objects.desc: Tin oxide ore. The only common source of tin, needed for bronze.

objects.name: Hematite
objects.desc: Red iron oxide. The workhorse iron ore.

objects.name: Magnetite
objects.desc: Magnetic black iron ore. Rich, but stubborn to smelt.

objects.name: Limonite
objects.desc: Bog iron, yellow-brown hydrated iron ore. Lean but shallow.

objects.name: Galena
objects.desc: Lead sulphide ore, smelts to lead, and to silver when worked finely.

objects.name: Native Gold
objects.desc: Raw gold nuggets and flakes. Rare; smelts straight to gold.

objects.name: Electrum Ore
objects.desc: Natural gold-silver alloy ore. Rare prestige metal source.

objects.name: Copper Bar
objects.desc: Smelted copper ingot. First metal, soft tools, wire, and half of bronze.

objects.name: Tin Bar
objects.desc: Smelted tin ingot. Soft on its own; alloyed with copper makes bronze.

objects.name: Bronze Bar
objects.desc: Cast bronze ingot, copper and tin. Tier-1 tools, weapons, and the first saw.

objects.name: Raw Sinew
objects.desc: Tendon pulled from the leg and back of a carcass, still wet and stiffening as it cools. It has to be dried hard and shredded down before it is any use as thread.

objects.name: Wool Yarn
objects.desc: Fleece carded straight and drawn onto the spindle. Springy, warm to handle, and the only form a loom will take wool in.

objects.name: Cotton Thread
objects.desc: Boll fibre picked clean of seed and spun fine. Takes dye better than flax and wears softer against skin.

objects.name: Fireclay Crucible
objects.desc: A squat pot thrown from refractory clay and fired until it rings. It will sit in a hearth holding liquid metal and come out unmarked, which is more than can be said for anything else in the colony.

objects.name: Rune-Sealed Flask
objects.desc: Glass held together by a binding cut into its own surface rather than by the glass itself. What goes in stops touching the walls, so nothing it carries can eat, burn or crack its way out.

objects.name: Molten Copper
objects.desc: The red metal run to liquid, skinned over with dark oxide that a stir breaks open. Pour it into a mould or let the hearth go cold and take it back as a bar.

objects.name: Molten Tin
objects.desc: Runs at a heat that barely reddens the hearth, and pours thin and quick as water. Pour it into a mould or let the hearth go cold and take it back as a bar.

objects.name: Molten Bronze
objects.desc: Copper and tin gone into one another for good. It fills a mould sharper than either alone, which is the whole reason for the alloy. Pour it into a mould or let the hearth go cold and take it back as a bar.

objects.name: Molten Lead
objects.desc: Sullen, heavy and slow to move, giving off a fume nobody should be standing over. Pour it into a mould or let the hearth go cold and take it back as a bar.

objects.name: Molten Silver
objects.desc: Bright to the point of hurting when the dross is drawn back off it. Pour it into a mould or let the hearth go cold and take it back as a bar.

objects.name: Molten Gold
objects.desc: So heavy it seems to lie lower in the crucible than it should. Nothing dulls it, not even the fire. Pour it into a mould or let the hearth go cold and take it back as a bar.

objects.name: Iron Bar
objects.desc: An ingot still freckled with slag from the hearth it was worked out of. Soft, tough and endlessly forgeable, the everyday iron.

objects.name: Wrought Iron
objects.desc: Iron drawn back out of pig metal and worked until the slag runs out in threads. Cleaner and more even than anything a bloomery gives up.

objects.name: Iron Nail
objects.desc: A handful of forged iron nails. Fasten planks into chests, furniture and frames. Drawn out on the smithy anvil.

objects.name: Copper Tack
objects.desc: Soft copper hammered into short tacks. The first metal fastener, holding boards where cordage would only lash them.

objects.name: Bronze Nail
objects.desc: A handful of cast bronze nails and tacks. The bronze-age fastener, pins planks into doors, floors and furniture before iron is smelted.

objects.name: Steel Rivet
objects.desc: Drawn steel rivets and bands. The high-tier fastener, binds reinforced walls, steel frames and runed apparatus where rope and nails would fail.

objects.name: Crucible Steel
objects.desc: High-carbon steel melted in a sealed crucible until it runs the same all through. Takes the finest edge there is, and is unforgiving if worked badly.

objects.name: Mechanism
objects.desc: An assembly of cut steel gears, axles and pins. The building block of mechanical power, links a waterwheel or windmill to the workstation it drives, and the heart of any clockwork device.

objects.name: Lead Bar
objects.desc: Smelted lead. Heavy, soft, pipes, weights, and shot.

objects.name: Silver Bar
objects.desc: Cupelled silver from galena. Coin, fine decor, and trade.

objects.name: Gold Bar
objects.desc: Cast gold ingot. Currency, prestige decor, and magical work.

objects.name: Pig Iron
objects.desc: Brittle, carbon-soaked iron run straight from the blast furnace. It pours beautifully and snaps under a hammer, so it is cast, never forged.

objects.name: Bloom Steel
objects.desc: Steel carburised straight in the bloom, uneven from one end of the bar to the other. The first steel a smith can make, and it shows.

objects.name: Blister Steel
objects.desc: Wrought iron baked for days packed in charcoal until the surface rises in blisters. Springy and keen, if still coarse at heart.

objects.name: Shear Steel
objects.desc: Blister steel cut, stacked and forge-welded back together until the carbon runs even. The blade smith's working stock.

objects.name: Mild Steel
objects.desc: Low-carbon steel puddled out in quantity. It will not take a fine edge, but it bends rather than shatters and comes by the cartload.

objects.name: Pattern-Welded Steel
objects.desc: Soft iron and hard steel folded through one another until the bar ripples like water. Days at the anvil for a piece that neither bends nor breaks.

objects.name: Ash
objects.desc: Wood ash from a fire. Used to cure hides and, later, to make lye and soap.

objects.name: Salt
objects.desc: Rock salt, ground fine. Preserves meat and cures hides, moderately rare, mined in the mountains.

objects.name: Water
objects.desc: Clean drinking water, drawn from a river/well or boiled and kept in a clay urn. Quenches thirst.

objects.name: Waterskin
objects.desc: A stitched leather bag for water, light, and holds a fair few sips. Fill it at a drink zone and carry it so you needn't trek to the river every time you're parched.

objects.name: Flask
objects.desc: A small stoppered flask of fired clay. Less than a skin, but cheap and sturdy.

objects.name: Tallow
objects.desc: Rendered fat, set hard in a pale block. Fuel for torches and lamps; later, soap.

objects.name: Torch
objects.desc: A branch wrapped in fat-soaked fibre. Burns for a while, giving light to work after dark.

objects.name: Tallow Candle
objects.desc: A fibre wick in moulded tallow. Longer, dimmer light than a torch.

objects.name: Smoked Fish
objects.desc: Split, brined overnight and hung a day in cold birch smoke. The smoke keeps the flies off and the flesh firm, and it will still be good long after the catch it came from would have gone.

objects.name: Smoked Meat
objects.desc: Strips hung in the smoke until they are dark and firm all the way through. Chewy, faintly bitter, and it will not turn on you for weeks.

objects.name: Smoked Ham
objects.desc: A whole hind leg salted, then hung in cold smoke for days. The outside goes near black; carve in and it is deep red and sweet.

objects.name: Smoked Sausage
objects.desc: Chopped meat and fat packed into gut and hung over the smoke. Firm enough to slice, greasy enough to keep.

objects.name: Smoked Cheese
objects.desc: A hard round left in the smoke until the rind turns amber. The smoke seals it as much as it flavours it.

objects.name: Salt Pork
objects.desc: Boar cut into fist-sized pieces and packed down in a barrel under its own brine. It comes out grey and needs a long soak before anyone will eat it, and it will still be there next spring.

objects.name: Pickled Vegetables
objects.desc: Cabbage and turnip packed in a crock under salt until they sour on their own. Sharp, cold and eaten all winter by people who would rather not lose their teeth.

objects.name: Hard Cheese
objects.desc: Curd pressed under a stone, salted and turned in the dark for months until the rind goes hard as bark. A wheel is a season's milk you can carry.

objects.name: Cured Ham
objects.desc: A whole hind leg buried in salt for a month, washed, and hung in the rafters for a year. It is the single most valuable thing most farmhouses own and it is eaten in slivers.

objects.name: Dry Sausage
objects.desc: Trimmings and fat chopped fine, salted hard, packed into gut and hung until it has lost a third of its weight. Every scrap the butcher could not sell, made to last a year.

objects.name: Potted Meat
objects.desc: Meat cooked down to threads, packed into a crock and sealed under a finger of set tallow. Break the seal and it must be eaten; leave it and it waits.

objects.name: Fruit Preserve
objects.desc: Berries boiled down with honey until a spoon stands in it, then sealed hot in a crock. Sweet enough that nothing will grow in it, which is the trick.

objects.name: Milk
objects.desc: Drawn warm and kept in the coolest corner of the house, where it has about a week before it turns. Almost everything worth keeping starts here.

objects.name: Salted Meat
objects.desc: Meat packed in salt. Keeps for a very long time.

objects.name: Dried Meat
objects.desc: Wind- and smoke-dried meat. Keeps well without salt.

objects.name: Dried Fruit
objects.desc: Apples, berries and grapes shrivelled sweet in the sun and smoke. Keeps for months without spoiling.

objects.name: Pine Plank
objects.desc: Sawn pine board. Furniture, floors, sturdy walls and roofs.

objects.name: Hewn Beam
objects.desc: A log squared off with an axe, heavy structural timber, hewn long before anyone could saw a plank. The frame of ropewalks, granaries, looms and benches.

objects.name: Oak Plank
objects.desc: Sawn oak board. Premium furniture and heavy framing.

objects.name: Birch Plank
objects.desc: Sawn birch board. Light furniture and panelling.

objects.name: Ash Plank
objects.desc: Sawn ash board. Springy and strong for shields and hafts.

objects.name: Willow Plank
objects.desc: Sawn willow board. Light and cheap panelling, soft and not for heavy framing.

objects.name: Yew Plank
objects.desc: Sawn yew board. Prized for bows and fine work.

objects.name: Saw
objects.desc: A toothed bronze blade in a wooden frame. Unlocks the sawtable and plank production.

objects.name: Granite
objects.desc: Hard igneous rock, the common building stone. Strong walls and prestige stonework.

objects.name: Limestone
objects.desc: Soft sedimentary rock. Mortar, and the smelting flux iron-making depends on.

objects.name: Sandstone
objects.desc: Soft, cheap sedimentary rock. Bulk building and decorative work.

objects.name: Marble
objects.desc: Prestige stone, statues and fine floors. Slow to cut.

objects.name: Slate
objects.desc: Flat-splitting stone. Roofing tiles and paving.

objects.name: Granite Block
objects.desc: Dressed granite block. Strong walls and prestige stonework.

objects.name: Limestone Block
objects.desc: Dressed limestone block. Soft, easy walls and mortar work.

objects.name: Sandstone Block
objects.desc: Dressed sandstone block. Cheap bulk building.

objects.name: Marble Block
objects.desc: Dressed marble block. Statues, fine floors, prestige decor.

objects.name: Slate Tile
objects.desc: Split slate roofing tile, the durable, low-maintenance roof.

objects.name: Blue Clay
objects.desc: Raw earthenware clay dug from a clay, mud or bog bank. The bulk ceramics and construction material.

objects.name: Fire Clay
objects.desc: Pale refractory clay dug from rare seams. Withstands forge heat, the raw stock for fire bricks, crucibles and casting molds.

objects.name: Sand
objects.desc: Loose grit gathered from dry savanna soil. Abrasive, a mold-facing for casting, and the future raw stock for glass.

objects.name: Sphagnum Moss
objects.desc: Soft absorbent bog moss. Packs wounds, lines bedding, and dries into ready tinder.

objects.name: Cordage
objects.desc: Twisted plant fiber. Thin makeshift cord, fine for binding, lashing and weaving, but too weak for real load.

objects.name: Rope
objects.desc: Strong laid rope, walked and twisted from many strands of cordage. Bears real load, well windlasses, rigging, heavy hauling.

objects.name: Mud Brick
objects.desc: Sun-dried mud brick. Requires no kiln.

objects.name: Fired Brick
objects.desc: Kiln-fired clay brick. Hard and weatherproof, forges, kilns, cellars, sturdy walls.

objects.name: Fire Brick
objects.desc: Refractory brick fired from fire clay. Withstands forge and kiln heat that would crack ordinary brick, the lining for high-heat furnaces.

objects.name: Urn
objects.desc: Fired clay vessel. Stores boiled water (and dry goods) safely. Keeps stored food longer (−20% spoilage).

objects.name: Clay Mold
objects.desc: Fired clay ingot mold. Required to cast metal bars, cracks and wears with each pour.

objects.name: Tile Mold
objects.desc: Cast-metal form for pressing clay roof tiles. Made at the forge, needs bronze.

objects.name: Clay Roof Tile
objects.desc: Pressed-and-fired clay tile. The durable, low-maintenance roof, slow to weather, robust against storms. (Pressing needs a reusable tile_mold, enforced once mold-required logic lands.)

objects.name: Flint Knife
objects.desc: Knapped flint blade. Cuts hide, prepares meat, required for Tier 1 crafts.

objects.name: Flint Sickle
objects.desc: Knapped flint chips set along a curved branch. Reaps grain and tends crops faster than bare hands, a field hand's flint knife.

objects.name: Stone Chopper
objects.desc: A large flaked stone with one heavy chopping edge, lashed to a stub of branch, the first crude cleaver. Hacks through joint and sinew to render a carcass and quarters meat for the pot; it still roughs out kindling and planks, and swung in anger its weight bites bare flesh, though it skids off any armour. Clumsy and brittle, but it is the edge you have.

objects.name: Digging Stick
objects.desc: Fire-hardened digging rod. Improves clay and root yield. Also used for basic fishing.

objects.name: Stone Axe
objects.desc: Hafted flint axe head. Required for felling trees. Brittle, good for only a handful of fells.

objects.name: Copper Axe
objects.desc: A cast copper head lashed to a branch. Fells faster than a knapped-stone axe, but the soft edge rolls and blunts — it wants re-grinding after only a few trees.

objects.name: Copper Pick
objects.desc: A copper point on a branch haft. Wins ore and soft stone quicker than a stone pick, but the metal is too soft to bite hard iron-bearing rock — and it blunts fast.

objects.name: Copper Knife
objects.desc: A cast copper blade with a wrapped grip. Holds an edge better than flint for skinning and butchering — until it dulls, which a soft copper edge does quickly.

objects.name: Copper Dagger
objects.desc: A leaf-shaped copper blade riveted to a bone grip — the first metal weapon, prized and buried with its owner. Soft: it bends on a hard block and needs straightening.

objects.name: Iron Axe
objects.desc: A forged iron felling axe. Bites deep, fells faster and lasts far longer than stone, and is hard enough to work the ancient hardwoods.

objects.name: Steel Axe
objects.desc: A tempered steel felling axe. Holds an edge through the densest ironwood, the woodsman's finest tool.

objects.name: Stone Hammer
objects.desc: Heavy stone maul. Drives stakes and beats earth, a builder works noticeably faster swinging one than with bare hands.

objects.name: Iron Hammer
objects.desc: A forged iron claw hammer. Drives and pulls nails cleanly, builds far faster than a stone maul and lasts a whole season of work.

objects.name: Steel Hammer
objects.desc: A tempered steel framing hammer, balanced and true. The fastest build tool a mundane colony can forge, and all but unbreakable.

objects.name: Stone Pick
objects.desc: A pointed stone hafted to a handle, the first tool that bites into rock and ore. Brittle; good for a handful of digs before it shatters.

objects.name: Stone Hoe
objects.desc: A flat stone blade lashed crosswise to a haft, for breaking soil and tending planted ground.

objects.name: Stone Spear
objects.desc: Flint-tipped wooden shaft. First proper hunting weapon.

objects.name: Stone Spade
objects.desc: Flat-bladed stone spade. Earth-moving and clay extraction, digs far faster than a bare digging stick.

objects.name: Iron Shovel
objects.desc: A forged iron shovel. Cuts through packed earth and clay with ease, far faster and longer-lived than a stone spade.

objects.name: Steel Shovel
objects.desc: A tempered steel shovel. Bites into the hardest ground and keeps its edge, the digger's finest tool.

objects.name: Iron Hoe
objects.desc: A forged iron hoe. Turns and tills soil far faster than a stone blade, and holds its edge through a whole season.

objects.name: Steel Hoe
objects.desc: A tempered steel hoe. Slices through root-bound earth effortlessly, the farmer's finest tool.

objects.name: Clay Cooking Pot
objects.desc: Rough clay vessel. Fire-tempered in the campfire. Enables stew and soup recipes.

objects.name: Carry-Basket
objects.desc: A woven basket lugged under one arm. The cheapest hauling aid there is: less to it than a backframe and it ties up a hand, but it doubles what comes back from a trip.

objects.name: Chest
objects.desc: A planked chest nailed together with iron. The sturdiest storage tier, 40 slots, keeps goods dry and food longer (−30% spoilage). Needs planks and forged nails.

objects.name: Wolf Carcass
objects.desc: A slain wolf. Skin and process it for hide and meat.

objects.name: Great Wolf Carcass
objects.desc: The body of a legendary dire wolf, near the size of a horse. A trophy — and a great deal of prime hide.

objects.name: Dire Wolf Pelt
objects.desc: A vast grey pelt, thick as a bearskin and stranger to the touch. Cured and worked, it holds a moonlit chill.

objects.name: Alpha Ichor
objects.desc: Dark, near-black blood drawn hot from a pack-leader's heart. The alchemists say it still runs when the beast is long dead.

objects.name: Owlbear Bile
objects.desc: A viscous amber humour from an owlbear's gut. Foul, potent, and prized by anyone brewing something that hardens flesh.

objects.name: Alpha's Heart
objects.desc: The dark, heavy heart of a pack-leader, still warm hours after the kill. Old hunters swallowed one raw to borrow the beast's fury — and were never quite themselves again.

objects.name: Direwolf Hackles
objects.desc: A ridge of coarse iron-grey hackles torn from a direwolf's nape. Chewed and swallowed, they leave the flesh strangely tough — and the mind a little wilder.

objects.name: Sabretooth Glands
objects.desc: Swollen scent-glands from behind a great cat's jaw, reeking of the kill. Something in them sharpens the urge to finish what you start.

objects.name: Owlbear Third Eye
objects.desc: A pale, pearl-like gland from deep in an owlbear's skull. Those who dare eat it speak of the world turning suddenly sharp and loud, and never wholly quiet again.

objects.name: Bloodrage Draught
objects.desc: A hot, coppery draught that sets the pulse hammering. For a while fear falls away and the arm swings faster and harder.

objects.name: Ironhide Tonic
objects.desc: A thick amber tonic that settles heavy in the gut. For a while the flesh holds firm and the body tires slow.

objects.name: Vigor Draught
objects.desc: A warm, iron-rich cordial pressed from bloodroot. It puts the colour back in a grey face and steadies a failing body.

objects.name: Calming Draught
objects.desc: A cool infusion of dreamleaf that quiets the racing mind. The knots in a person loosen and the breath comes slow.

objects.name: Nightglow Draught
objects.desc: A luminous blue tincture drawn from glowcaps. The dark thins and the edges of things come clear where there is no light to see by.

objects.name: Frenzy Draught
objects.desc: A distillation of madness-spore, thick and grey. It sets the blood roaring and the reason sleeping — for a while there is only the fight.

objects.name: Venom Coating
objects.desc: A thick black paste of rendered venom-sac and nightshade, brushed along an edge. It clings to the steel and rides the next cut into the wound.

objects.name: Caustic Bile
objects.desc: Acrid green humour wrung from a bog ooze, still faintly hissing. It eats at leather and skin alike, so it is kept in a sealed clay pot.

objects.name: Caustic Coating
objects.desc: Bog bile cooked down with nightshade into a clinging grey slime. Smeared on an edge, it turns the smallest cut foul and roils the stomach.

objects.name: Crude Feral Draught
objects.desc: A pack-heart boiled raw with bloodroot. It floods the veins with borrowed fury, and takes its own cut of the drinker in return.

objects.name: Feral Transfusion
objects.desc: The alpha-heart humour drawn off clean and cut with spirit. The fury runs truer now, though the body still pays.

objects.name: Alpha's Essence
objects.desc: A distilled heart-essence, patient work of the apothecary. At its best it wakes the whole beast in a person, and asks little back.

objects.name: Crude Hide Draught
objects.desc: Ground hackles simmered in tallow. The skin thickens and dulls to pain, but the change comes rough.

objects.name: Hide Transfusion
objects.desc: The hackle-humour rendered and refined. The hide sets harder, sometimes scaling over like a beast's own plate.

objects.name: Ironhide Essence
objects.desc: A perfected toughening draught. At its finest the flesh turns near to iron, and the drinker walks away whole.

objects.name: Crude Predator Draught
objects.desc: Scent-glands mashed with nightshade. The urge to finish the kill sharpens, and something human dulls.

objects.name: Predator Transfusion
objects.desc: The glandular draught drawn off cleaner. The hands learn to tear as much as strike.

objects.name: Sabretooth Essence
objects.desc: A refined predator-essence. At its peak it lends the whole hunting beast, its teeth and its patience both.

objects.name: Crude Sight Draught
objects.desc: A third eye steeped in glowcap. The senses widen and swim, and the head aches for it.

objects.name: Sight Transfusion
objects.desc: The pineal humour refined. The dark thins and the ears reach further, sometimes past what the mind wants to hear.

objects.name: Third-Eye Essence
objects.desc: A clarified sight-essence. At its clearest nothing moves unseen near the drinker, and the price is slight.

objects.name: Greater Potion of Might
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the potion of might, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Potion of Might
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the potion of might, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Greater Draught of Vigor
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the draught of vigor, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Draught of Vigor
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the draught of vigor, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Greater Elixir of Grace
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the elixir of grace, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Elixir of Grace
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the elixir of grace, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Greater Tonic of Fortitude
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the tonic of fortitude, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Tonic of Fortitude
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the tonic of fortitude, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the bloodrage draught, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Bloodrage Draught
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the bloodrage draught, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the ironhide tonic, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Ironhide Tonic
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the ironhide tonic, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the vigor draught, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Vigor Draught
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the vigor draught, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Calming Draught
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the calming draught, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the nightglow draught, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Nightglow Draught
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the nightglow draught, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.
