objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the frenzy draught, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Frenzy Draught
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the frenzy draught, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Greater Venom Coating
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the venom coating, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Venom Coating
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the venom coating, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Greater Caustic Coating
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the caustic coating, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Caustic Coating
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the caustic coating, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Direwolf Warcloak
objects.desc: A cloak of cured dire-wolf pelt, worked at a magical loom. It sits on the shoulders like a living thing and lends the wearer a beast's strength.

objects.name: Stargazer's Circlet
objects.desc: A slender band set with a shard of fallen star, cold against the brow. The world sharpens around the one who wears it — a sound, a scent, a movement at the edge of sight.

objects.name: Dire Wolf Carcass
objects.desc: A wolf half again the size it has any right to be. The pelt alone is worth the fight.

objects.name: Cave Bear Carcass
objects.desc: A mountain of dead bear. Skinning it is a day's work; wasting it would be a sin.

objects.name: Direboar Carcass
objects.desc: A tusker the size of a cart. Bristle, fat, ivory and fury, in that order.

objects.name: Broodmother Carcass
objects.desc: A great spider, curled in death. The silk glands and venom sacs are still full.

objects.name: Great Bear Carcass
objects.desc: The body of a legendary bear, vast as a toppled standing stone. Songs will argue over who felled it.

objects.name: Great Boar Carcass
objects.desc: The body of a legendary boar, scarred by a hundred failed hunts that ended worse for the hunters.

objects.name: Great Weaver Carcass
objects.desc: The body of a legendary spider queen. Even dead, the web around it seems to listen.

objects.name: Cave Bear Pelt
objects.desc: A pelt broad enough to roof a tent, with guard hairs like wire. Warmth for a winter and armour besides.

objects.name: Great Fang
objects.desc: A canine tooth the length of a forearm, taken from something that ruled its ground. Hard as flint and holds an edge.

objects.name: Great Bone
objects.desc: A leg bone thick as a roof beam, from a beast of legend. A haft made of it never breaks first.

objects.name: Great Tusk
objects.desc: A sweep of ivory taller than the hunter who claimed it. Carvers and kings pay dearly for such a thing.

objects.name: Venom Sac
objects.desc: A taut gland of pale venom, cut whole from behind the fangs. Handled with more care than most treasure.

objects.name: Cave-Bear Plate
objects.desc: Boiled cave-bear hide over an iron frame, worked at a magical bench. It carries the mountain-calm of the beast it came from.

objects.name: Fang-Reaver
objects.desc: A great fang set in a heartwood haft, bound with sinew and older words. It bites as its first owner did, and lends the arm behind it a beast's strength.

objects.name: Bear Carcass
objects.desc: A massive cave bear. Butcher it for prime cuts, hide, and fat.

objects.name: Goblin Remains
objects.desc: A fallen goblin. Mostly bone and leather scraps.

objects.name: Giant Rat Carcass
objects.desc: A large dead rat. Lean, gamey meat if you're not picky.

objects.name: Boar Carcass
objects.desc: A slain wild boar. Process for meat, bone, and tusks.

objects.name: Elk Carcass
objects.desc: A large elk. Yields generous cuts of venison, hide, and antler.

objects.name: Mountain Goat Carcass
objects.desc: A mountain goat. Modest meat yield; hide is tough and durable.

objects.name: Wild Chicken Carcass
objects.desc: A plucked wild chicken. Small but worth the effort.

objects.name: Aurochs Carcass
objects.desc: A felled aurochs, a massive wild ox. Prime beef, heavy hide, and horn.

objects.name: Woolly Mammoth Carcass
objects.desc: A toppled mammoth. Enormous yield of meat, shaggy wool, hide, and ivory.

objects.name: Hippogriff Carcass
objects.desc: A slain hippogriff. Lean fowl-and-horse meat, feathers, and hide.

objects.name: Hoarfowl Carcass
objects.desc: A giant ground bird. Plenty of pale meat and a heap of down.

objects.name: Quillback Carcass
objects.desc: A large quilled rodent. Modest gamey meat; the quills are useful too.

objects.name: Worg Carcass
objects.desc: A great dire-wolf. Tough, stringy meat and a thick grey pelt.

objects.name: Jackal Carcass
objects.desc: A scrawny scavenger. Little meat, a thin hide.

objects.name: Owlbear Carcass
objects.desc: A monstrous owlbear. Heaps of meat, a shaggy feathered hide, and claws.

objects.name: Sabretooth Carcass
objects.desc: A great sabre-fanged cat. Lean meat, a prized striped hide, and fangs.

objects.name: Mire Crocodile Carcass
objects.desc: A slain mire crocodile. Dense meat and a thick scaled hide.

objects.name: Marsh Viper Carcass
objects.desc: A long swamp serpent. A little meat, a supple skin, and venom glands.

objects.name: Stirge Carcass
objects.desc: A bloated blood-drinking flyer. Barely worth skinning.

objects.name: Grimeling Residue
objects.desc: The collapsed muck of a slain grimeling. Foul sludge and fibrous matter.

objects.name: Giant Olm Carcass
objects.desc: A pale blind amphibian. Soft, oily flesh, edible if you must.

objects.name: Thornwood Spider Carcass
objects.desc: A great forest spider. Chitin, silk glands, and venom, little meat.

objects.name: Kobold Remains
objects.desc: A fallen kobold. Scrawny, mostly bone and scavenged scraps.

objects.name: Gnoll Remains
objects.desc: A slain hyena-folk marauder. Sinewy frame, coarse pelt.

objects.name: Orc Remains
objects.desc: A fallen orc reaver. Heavy, muscular frame and crude leathers.

objects.name: Harpy Carcass
objects.desc: A downed harpy. Wretched meat, but the wing feathers are fine.

objects.name: Bullywug Remains
objects.desc: A slain frog-folk skirmisher. Clammy hide and stringy leg meat.

objects.name: Wolf Meat
objects.desc: Tough, gamey predator meat. Edible if well-seasoned.

objects.name: Bear Meat
objects.desc: Rich, fatty bear meat. Dense and warming.

objects.name: Boar Meat
objects.desc: Robust, well-marbled wild pork. Excellent in stew.

objects.name: Elk Meat
objects.desc: Lean, premium venison from a large elk.

objects.name: Goat Meat
objects.desc: Lean mountain goat. Mild flavour, modest portion.

objects.name: Chicken Meat
objects.desc: Delicate wild chicken. Small but flavourful.

objects.name: Rat Meat
objects.desc: Gamey and unpleasant. Better than starving.

objects.name: Rabbit Pelt
objects.desc: Small, soft rabbit pelt. Light insulation and trim.

objects.name: Deer Hide
objects.desc: Supple deer skin. A foundational leatherworking material.

objects.name: Wolf Hide
objects.desc: Coarse wolf skin with a dense undercoat. Excellent for cold-weather gear.

objects.name: Jackal Hide
objects.desc: Thin, sandy jackal skin. Little warmth in it, but it stays light in dry heat.

objects.name: Bear Pelt
objects.desc: Thick, shaggy bear pelt. Premium winter cloak material.

objects.name: Boar Hide
objects.desc: Thick, bristle-covered boar skin. Stiff but durable.

objects.name: Elk Hide
objects.desc: Large, tough elk hide. Ideal for armour lining and tents.

objects.name: Goat Hide
objects.desc: Tough mountain goat hide. Weather-resistant and hard-wearing.

objects.name: Chicken Feathers
objects.desc: Soft wild-chicken feathers. Stuffing, fletching, and decoration.

objects.name: Rat Pelt
objects.desc: Small, coarse rat skin. Barely worth the scraping.

objects.name: Small Bones
objects.desc: Hollow, delicate bones from small animals. Useful for needles and fishhooks.

objects.name: Medium Bones
objects.desc: Sturdy mid-sized bones. Blanched into tools, handles, and toggles.

objects.name: Large Bones
objects.desc: Massive load-bearing bones. Ground for fertiliser or carved into heavy tools.

objects.name: Rotten Food
objects.desc: Spoiled plant matter, fish, or cooked food. Causes illness if eaten.

objects.name: Rotten Meat
objects.desc: Putrefied raw meat. Dangerous to consume. Still useful as animal bait.

objects.name: Rotten Carcass
objects.desc: A fully decomposed animal body. Inedible. Can be worked into fertiliser.

objects.name: Carcass
objects.desc: The mortal remains of one of your own. Bury or haul them; do not leave them to the crows.

objects.name: Unconscious Body
objects.desc: A downed colonist slung over a rescuer's shoulders, being carried to safety.

objects.name: Bone Cleaver
objects.desc: A heavy blade split from large animal bone and knapped to a sharp edge, lashed to a hardwood grip with cordage. Renders noticeably more yield from any carcass than a flint knife.

objects.name: Butcher's Kit
objects.desc: A roll of iron skinning knives, boning hooks and a fine-toothed saw, laced into a leather satchel. The set for opening a big beast cleanly, where a single blade would bind and tear.

objects.name: Flensing Kit
objects.desc: Steel blades, gambrels and a bone saw laid in a fitted leather roll and buckled shut. A full field-dressing set that strips even the rarest carcass down to its last useful organ.

objects.name: Bone Fleshing Scraper
objects.desc: A shoulder-blade ground to a blunt draw-edge and hafted to a branch. Dragged down a raw skin over a beam, it lifts away the fat and membrane that would otherwise rot the hide — the blunt edge peels where a keen knife would slit.

objects.name: Iron Fleshing Knife
objects.desc: A broad two-handled draw-blade of iron, curved to ride a beam. Strips a hide clean in a fraction of the passes a bone scraper needs, and bites through the heavy fat of a beast pelt.

objects.name: Currier's Kit
objects.desc: Slicker, stakes and a set of iron graining boards for working tanned leather supple — stretching, oiling and boning the fibres until a stiff crust becomes a hide that drapes and holds a stitch.

objects.name: Steel Currier's Kit
objects.desc: Fine steel slickers and graining boards that finish even the toughest beast leather glassy-smooth, drawing the most out of every rare prime hide.

objects.name: Sewing Kit
objects.desc: Iron needles, an awl and waxed thread in a folded roll — the set for stitching cut leather and cloth into finished garments, where a raw seam would gape and pull loose.

objects.name: Tailor's Kit
objects.desc: Fine steel needles, shears and a bodkin in a fitted case — the set for tailored work, close seams and set sleeves a plain sewing kit can only approximate.

objects.name: Wooden Haft
objects.desc: A branch shaved and carved to seat a socket or tang snug. Sound enough for a copper or bronze head, where a raw stick would work loose.

objects.name: Sanded Haft
objects.desc: A carved haft rubbed smooth with sandstone and grit — no splinters to raise, and the open grain ready to drink in a seasoning soak.

objects.name: Emberwood Haft
objects.desc: Split down the grain and turned true, warm under the hand the way the standing tree was. The heat is in the wood, not on it.

objects.name: Moonwood Haft
objects.desc: Pale and close-grained, worked while green and left to set hard. It stays cold to hold no matter how long it is carried.

objects.name: Heartwood Haft
objects.desc: Cut from the dense core where the rings crowd together, then shaved down over days. It does not flex and it does not split.

objects.name: Seasoned Haft
objects.desc: A sanded haft soaked and cured until the grain is set hard and water-tight. It takes the shock of an iron or steel head without splitting — the handle a real tool is worth building on.

objects.name: Green-Wood Tongs
objects.desc: A bent length of soaked green wood, lashed at the bend. Lets you hold hot metal at the forge, until the heat chars through it. Crude, short-lived, but it gets the first bars worked.

objects.name: Iron Tongs
objects.desc: Forged iron tongs with a riveted pivot. Grip hot stock all day without charring, the proper smith's tool.

objects.name: Steel Tongs
objects.desc: Spring-steel tongs that hold their set and outlast the smith. The last pair of tongs you'll ever forge.

objects.name: Fists
objects.desc: Bare knuckles. Frequent and cheap, and a knuckle drives into an eye or a throat as surely as a claw.

objects.name: Kick
objects.desc: A booted heel. Rarer than a jab, hits harder, staggers, tires faster.

objects.name: Bite
objects.desc: Teeth. Crit-prone piercing attack.

objects.name: Claw
objects.desc: Raking claws. Fast cutting swipes that open wounds.

objects.name: Slam
objects.desc: A heavy body blow. Big blunt hit, strong knockdown.

objects.name: Tusk
objects.desc: Goring tusks. Deep piercing wounds.

objects.name: Charge
objects.desc: A full-body charge. Heavy blunt impact, brutal knockdown.

objects.name: Boar Tusk
objects.desc: Short, curved boar tusks. Goring slashes, far less reach than a great beast's tusks.

objects.name: Boar Charge
objects.desc: A low, barrelling charge. Solid blunt impact, but nothing like a bull's.

objects.name: Antler
objects.desc: Sharp antler points. Piercing gore.

objects.name: Headbutt
objects.desc: A skull-first ram. Blunt and staggering.

objects.name: Peck
objects.desc: A sharp beak jab. Tiny but quick.

objects.name: Spectral Strike
objects.desc: A chilling incorporeal blow that ignores flesh and rattles the bone.

objects.name: Venomous Bite
objects.desc: Fangs that sink venom with the wound. Crit-prone piercing strike with a chance to envenom (vipers, spiders).

objects.name: Virulent Bite
objects.desc: Fangs long as fingers, running with venom that blackens the wound. Few shrug off a full bite.

objects.name: Trample
objects.desc: The full weight of a great beast brought down through hoof and knee. Bones, shields and fences fare alike beneath it.

objects.name: Constrict
objects.desc: Coil upon coil drawing tight. What it holds does not run, and soon does not breathe easily either.

objects.name: Quill Volley
objects.desc: A shudder of the haunches and the air is full of quills — needle-sharp, loosed farther than any claw can swipe.

objects.name: Proboscis
objects.desc: A blood-drinking feeding stab. Little impact, but the wound won't clot, it bleeds and saps blood directly (stirges).

objects.name: Screech
objects.desc: An ear-splitting cry. Barely a blow, but it scrambles the senses of those who hear it (harpies).

objects.name: Snaring Tongue
objects.desc: A long, sticky tongue that lashes out and holds, pins the target in place for a beat (bullywugs).

objects.name: Rending Claws
objects.desc: Long curved claws that rake flesh open. A devastating unarmed strike that leaves bleeding wounds.

d.effect: DEX −1 · crafts spd ×0.75 · leatherworking spd ×0.8 · construction spd ×0.85

objects.name: Moonlit Claws
objects.desc: Claws that only come out under a full moon, long, pale and wickedly sharp. They open flesh like wet cloth.

objects.name: Goring Horns
objects.desc: A lowered head and a driving charge. Heavy horns that punch through and knock the target off their feet.

objects.name: Serpent Fangs
objects.desc: Hollow fangs that sink venom with the bite. A crit-prone piercing strike with a strong chance to envenom.

objects.name: Dragon Claws
objects.desc: Great draconic talons that shear through armor and flesh alike, leaving deep bleeding rents.

objects.name: Bloodsucking Fangs
objects.desc: A feeding bite that opens the vein and drinks. Little impact, but the wound won't clot and blood is drawn straight off.

objects.name: Flame Breath
objects.desc: A gout of dragonfire spat at a single foe, sears on contact and sets them alight. (Pass 1: single-target; the true cone is deferred.)

objects.name: Budding Claws
objects.desc: Short, hardened claw-nubs, a scraping unarmed strike, the first stage of a claw line.

objects.name: Ripping Talons
objects.desc: Great hooked talons that open flesh like cloth and leave wounds that will not close on their own.

d.effect: DEX −1 · crafts spd ×0.7 · leatherworking spd ×0.75 · construction spd ×0.8

objects.name: Goring Fangs
objects.desc: Long driving fangs, a deep, punching bite.

objects.name: Sabre Fangs
objects.desc: Immense sabre teeth that punch through and tear free, the wound bleeds until it is bound.

objects.name: Great Horns
objects.desc: A massive sweeping crown of horn, a goring charge that hurls the target off their feet.

objects.name: Great Tusks
objects.desc: Heavy curved tusks that punch deep and toss the struck aside.

objects.name: Deathly Fangs
objects.desc: Long hollow fangs running with a killing venom, few shrug off the bite.

objects.name: Ember Breath
objects.desc: A short spat gout of embers, sears a burn at arm's reach and can catch clothes alight.

objects.name: Dragonfire
objects.desc: A roaring lance of dragonfire that strikes three tiles out like a spear, sears a true burn, hurls the target back, and leaves them alight. (TODO: upgrade to a proper AoE cone.)

objects.name: Raking Talons
objects.desc: Curved raptor talons on the feet, a raking, slashing kick.

objects.name: Hooked Talons
objects.desc: Long hooked talons that seize and shear, a raptor's killing stroke.

objects.name: Raptor Talons
objects.desc: Immense sickle talons that disembowel, the rents they leave will not close unaided.

objects.name: Pecking Beak
objects.desc: A hard horn-cased mouth, a jabbing peck of a bite.

objects.name: Tearing Beak
objects.desc: A heavy hooked beak that tears rather than pecks.

objects.name: Rending Beak
objects.desc: A great shearing beak that strips flesh from bone.

objects.name: Crushing Claw
objects.desc: A massive shell-plated pincer, a slow crushing grip that caves armor and bone alike.

objects.name: Webbing
objects.desc: A flung lash of sticky silk that snares the target in place, control, not damage.

objects.name: Chilling Touch
objects.desc: A grave-cold grip that frost-burns flesh where it lands.

objects.name: Shock Touch
objects.desc: A crackling static discharge that scorches and staggers.

objects.name: Hide Tool-Roll
objects.desc: A strip of cured hide with thong loops, rolled up and tied to the belt to keep two or three small tools to hand. Crude, but it does the job.

objects.name: Hide Pouch
objects.desc: A plain pouch of cured hide pulled shut with a drawstring and hung from the belt. Holds a handful of gleanings and nothing more.

objects.name: Linen Satchel
objects.desc: A tube of coarse linen, drawn shut at both ends and slung across the back. The first thing that lets you haul a real load on foot.

objects.name: Wicker Frame
objects.desc: A lattice of withies bent and lashed into a backframe. Nothing about it bears weight for you; it just gives bulky goods somewhere to ride.

objects.name: Leather Knapsack
objects.desc: A sewn leather bag on two shoulder straps, its flap drawn down under cast buckles. It rides square and high, so the load sits over the hips instead of hanging off the shoulders.

objects.name: Steel-Riveted Knapsack
objects.desc: A tall leather pack lashed to a shaped wooden frame and riveted in steel at every strap end. It swallows more than anything else worn on a back, and it is still the wearer's own shoulders underneath.

objects.name: Rune-Stitched Knapsack
objects.desc: Leather closed with enchanted thread, every seam running a line of small cut glyphs that catch the light when the pack shifts. What goes into it stops pulling on the straps the way it did going in.

objects.name: Framed Leather Pack
objects.desc: Leather panels laced onto a bent wooden frame, tall enough to stand clear of the shoulders. It holds a load high off the back, and it catches on everything in close brush.

objects.name: Iron-Buckled Satchel
objects.desc: A flat leather bag on a single broad strap, closed with two iron buckles and worn across the body. It sits still against the ribs and leaves both hands and the whole back free.

objects.name: Iron-Buckled Knapsack
objects.desc: A squared leather pack on two shoulder straps, every strap end running through an iron buckle so the fit can be pulled down tight. The load stops shifting, which is most of what makes a long walk bearable.

objects.name: Iron-Framed Pack
objects.desc: A deep pack hung on a nailed wooden frame with iron corner straps, cut square so nothing packs around a curve. Awkward through a doorway and worth it for a haul of pelts.

objects.name: Steel-Buckled Satchel
objects.desc: Thick leather on a sprung steel buckle that opens under a thumb and holds through a run. Cut close to the body, quiet, and emptied without stopping.

objects.name: Steel-Framed Pack
objects.desc: A freighting pack on a riveted steel frame, deep enough to lose a week's stores in. It holds far more than one back can actually shift, which is how people end up making two trips anyway.

objects.name: Rune-Woven Satchel
objects.desc: Silk worked on the runed loom into a bag no deeper than a hand, which nonetheless takes an armload and keeps its shape. It hangs as though empty whatever is in it.

objects.name: Rune-Bound Frame Pack
objects.desc: A freighting frame of magic alloy, its uprights cut with binding glyphs and its panels stitched in enchanted thread. Space inside it runs out long after it should, and it is still walked up the hill by hand.

objects.name: Leather Belt
objects.desc: A wide sewn belt on a cast buckle with two pouches hung from it. Small things sit at the hip where a hand finds them without looking.

objects.name: Iron-Ringed Belt
objects.desc: Iron rings set at intervals along a doubled leather belt. A pouch, a knife, a cup and a coil of cord hang wherever their owner wants them, and a ring takes a wrench that would tear a stitched loop off.

objects.name: Steel-Buckled Tool-Belt
objects.desc: Broad, thick leather on a forged steel buckle, hung with loops, rings and a deep hip bag. About as much as will hang off a waist before it starts fouling the legs.

objects.name: Rune-Etched Belt
objects.desc: A broad belt plated in magic alloy and cut with glyphs from buckle to tail. Whatever hangs on it settles somewhere other than the wearer's back.

objects.name: Hide Knife-Sheath
objects.desc: A folded strip of cured hide stitched into a pocket for a blade and pushed onto the belt. The knife stops swinging, stops catching on brush, and stops being the loudest thing in the wood.

objects.name: Leather Sword-Belt
objects.desc: A belt with a sewn loop on the left hip and a scabbard hung through it. The hilt sits where the hand already is, and the blade lies quiet against the leg on the walk in.

objects.name: Iron-Mounted Sword-Belt
objects.desc: Belt and scabbard both dressed in iron at the buckle, the mouth and the tip. The sheath is pinned against the thigh, so a run does not set it slapping.

objects.name: Steel-Plated War-Belt
objects.desc: Steel plaques riveted along a doubled belt wide enough to cover the hip bones, with mounts for a scabbard and a dagger. There is barely a pouch on it; the plate is what it is for.

objects.name: Flint Handaxe
objects.desc: A hafted flint head. First proper melee weapon, cuts and splits.

objects.name: Wattle Buckler
objects.desc: A small woven wattle shield. Deflects blows but shatters quickly.

objects.name: Bone Splinter Knife
objects.desc: A sharp bone splinter bound with cordage. Lethal at close quarters.

objects.name: Antler War Club
objects.desc: A heavy antler lashed to a cordage grip. Breaks bones without cutting.

objects.name: Bone-Tipped Thrusting Spear
objects.desc: A wooden shaft tipped with a sharpened bone. Better reach than a knife.

objects.name: Bronze Punch Dagger
objects.desc: A cast bronze push-dagger with bone grip scales. Quick and deadly at close range.

objects.name: Leaf-Blade Spear
objects.desc: A cast bronze leaf-shaped blade on a hafted shaft. Two-handed reach weapon.

objects.name: Cast Bronze Hatchet
objects.desc: A cast bronze axe head on a wooden haft. Splits mail and bone alike.

objects.name: Self Bow
objects.desc: A simple stave bow cut from a single piece of wood. Range advantage over melee.

objects.name: Rawhide-Faced Round Shield
objects.desc: An oak plank shield faced with stretched rawhide. Solid Tier 1 defence.

objects.name: Plank Round Shield
objects.desc: Boards pegged edge to edge around a hand-hole and sanded smooth, with nothing laid over the face. Every solid blow works the seams a little further apart.

objects.name: Short Seax
objects.desc: A single-edged iron blade. The sidearm of every free warrior.

objects.name: Spatha
objects.desc: A long cavalry sword, balanced for cutting and thrusting alike.

objects.name: Bearded Axe
objects.desc: A wide-bellied iron axe. Hooks shields and splits helmets.

objects.name: Orc Cleaver
objects.desc: A slab of crude iron beaten to an edge, near as long as a man is tall. It takes a monster's arm to bring it round.

objects.name: Orc Maul
objects.desc: A haft of black iron capped with a jagged head. Made to cave in shields, gates, and skulls alike.

objects.name: Serrated Waraxe
objects.desc: Notched and re-notched until the edge tears more than it cuts. Heavy in a mortal hand, quick in a brute's.

objects.name: Orc Scrap Plate
objects.desc: Riveted plates hacked from a dozen fallen foes and lashed on without a care for the fit. Heavy, and it clatters.

objects.name: Goblin Shank
objects.desc: A sliver of scrap ground to a wicked point and smeared with something that festers.

objects.name: Hooked Jabber
objects.desc: A long shaft ending in a barbed hook — meant to drag a victim off their feet and open them on the way down.

objects.name: Weighted Net
objects.desc: Knotted cord and rusty weights. Does little harm, but a fouled foe stops running.

objects.name: Goblin Scrap Vest
objects.desc: Patches of boiled hide, bark and stolen cloth stitched over each other. Light, and barely armour at all.

objects.name: Gravemaker
objects.desc: A greatsword forged for a hand half again the size of yours, the grip rewound in strips of something that was recently attached to someone. It is heavier than it needs to be and that is the design.

objects.name: The Anvil-Breaker
objects.desc: A squared head of black iron on a haft bound with wire. It does not cut and it does not need to; what it hits stops being the shape it was.

objects.name: Great-Tusk Impaler
objects.desc: A boar's tusk the length of a forearm, split, ground to a point and socketed onto a seasoned shaft. The curve is what stops the thing you put it in from coming any further up it.

objects.name: The Flenser
objects.desc: A slab of a blade with a rolled spine and no point at all, ground to an edge along its whole length. It was made for taking a carcass apart and has never been asked to do anything else.

objects.name: Chainbiter
objects.desc: Three studded heads on separate chains. Nobody who carries one can tell you where the second and third are going, which is exactly why a shield is no comfort against it.

objects.name: Siege-Lock Arbalest
objects.desc: A steel prod on a windlass, built to be shot from behind a wall at things trying to come over it. Slow to wind and it does not care what you were wearing.

objects.name: Great-Fang Javelin
objects.desc: A fang lashed into a split haft and whipped tight. Heavy at the head and light behind it, so it turns over once and lands on the point.

objects.name: Great-Fang Dirk
objects.desc: A single fang, unworked but for the grip wound onto its root. It has no edge worth the name and does not need one; it was already the sharpest thing in the animal.

objects.name: Warren Hornbow
objects.desc: Horn and sinew laid back against a short wooden core, so it draws far heavier than its length suggests. Made to be shot from a crouch in a tunnel mouth.

objects.name: Skullcracker Sling
objects.desc: A long braided cord with a leather cradle stiffened by use. In the right hands a river stone out of it arrives faster than an arrow and hits like a hammer.

objects.name: Warren Needle
objects.desc: A thin stiff blade with a knuckle-guard of scrap, all point and no edge. Built for the half-second a shield comes off line.

objects.name: Orc Greataxe
objects.desc: Two crescents of black iron on a shaft cut for a hand far larger than a man's. In the right grip it shears through shield, mail and the arm beneath.

objects.name: The Iron Tide
objects.desc: A warlord's greataxe, black iron chased with copper, its edge kept by a hundred whetstones and a hundred more skulls. It falls like a wave and leaves as little standing.

objects.name: Iron Slab Shield
objects.desc: Less a shield than a door of riveted iron plate. Behind it an orc weathers a shieldwall; a lesser arm just tires holding it up.

objects.name: Orc Plate Vambraces
objects.desc: Slabs of hammered iron strapped over the forearm and left deliberately proud at the elbow, so a parry costs the other man something.

objects.name: Orc Plate Gauntlets
objects.desc: Plate over the back of the hand and nothing at all over the palm. Whoever made them cared about hitting and not about holding.

objects.name: Orc Plate Sabatons
objects.desc: Iron scales laced onto a heavy sole, toes capped and squared. They were not built for walking far.

objects.name: Great-Bone Helm
objects.desc: A skull plate off something enormous, cut down, boiled hard and lined with pelt. The ridge over the brow is where the animal's own was.

objects.name: Great-Bone Cuirass
objects.desc: Overlapping plates of boiled bone laced onto a cave bear's hide, each one taken whole off a beast that took a hunting party to bring down. Lighter than steel and it does not go cold in the night.

objects.name: Great-Bone Vambraces
objects.desc: Split lengths of legbone laid along the forearm and lashed through drilled holes, the hackles left on at the wrist.

objects.name: Great-Bone Greaves
objects.desc: Bone splints down the shin over a pelt lining, cut so the knee still bends the whole way.

objects.name: Great-Bone Gauntlets
objects.desc: Scales of bone stitched to hide across the back of the hand, claws left on at the knuckle.

objects.name: Great-Bone Sabatons
objects.desc: Bone plate over a fur boot, soled with the thick hide off the animal's own foot.

objects.name: Orc Warplate
objects.desc: Overlapping slabs of blackened iron hammered to an orc's barrel frame. Crude joins, brutal coverage — a walking wall that rings like a bell under blows.

objects.name: Goblin Poison Bow
objects.desc: A short recurve of scavenged horn and gut, its string black with old venom. Every arrow it looses carries a little of the swamp with it.

objects.name: Goblin Firepot
objects.desc: A clay pot of pitch and tallow with a smouldering wick, swung on a cord. It shatters against whatever it strikes and clings, burning.

objects.name: Kobold Trap-Spear
objects.desc: A long prod ending in a snare loop and a barbed point — made for pinning something bigger than its wielder while the rest of the warren closes in.

objects.name: Gnoll Bone Cleaver
objects.desc: The jawbone of something huge, split and edged with set flint teeth. Heavy, ugly, and it tears a wound that laughs at bandages.

objects.name: Gnoll Flint Axe
objects.desc: A hyena-headed axe of knapped flint lashed with rawhide, notched from years of raiding. Light enough to swing all night.

objects.name: Framea
objects.desc: A thrusting spear with a narrow iron head. Reach advantage and strong armour penetration.

objects.name: Great-Bone Maul
objects.desc: The thigh-bone of a great beast, banded and hafted into a crude two-handed maul. Heavier than any stone head, and it carries something of the creature's weight behind every swing.

objects.name: Stone Maul
objects.desc: A heavy hafted stone head. It doesn't cut, it breaks: bones, and the will of anything in armour.

objects.name: Iron Mace
objects.desc: A flanged iron head on a short haft. The flanges bite plate where an edge would skid, armour's answer in one hand, leaving the other for a shield.

objects.name: Iron Warhammer
objects.desc: A long-hafted hammer with a spiked poll. Two hands drive its full weight through any plate, the slow, certain crack of a knight undone.

objects.name: Iron Greatsword
objects.desc: A long iron blade gripped in both fists. Slow to bring around, but a strong arm cleaves men in two with it, no finesse, just weight and edge.

objects.name: Steel Longsword
objects.desc: A keen steel blade, balanced for one hand or two. Accurate, quick to recover, and forgiving, the all-rounder a swordsman grows into, and the base of the duelist's art.

objects.name: Steel Greatsword
objects.desc: A great two-handed steel blade. Ponderous, but a powerful arm puts its whole length through shield and man together, the high-STR slayer who needs no help to hit.

objects.name: Steel Pike
objects.desc: A long steel spear with a needle point. The truest weapon to land a blow, it finds the gap in any guard, but it only pricks where a sword would cleave.

objects.name: Steel Mace
objects.desc: A flanged steel head on a short haft. Accurate for a blunt weapon and a real plate-dinter, one hand, leaving the other for a shield.

objects.name: Steel Warhammer
objects.desc: A two-handed steel hammer with a hardened beak. Nothing wrecks armour faster, a few blows leave a knight in dented scrap, then the next lands on bare flesh.

objects.name: Steel Cleaver
objects.desc: A heavy single-edged chopper, all weight behind a wicked edge. No grace, it skids off plate and barely dents it, but on bare flesh it butchers, finding the killing blow again and again. The swordsman's brutal specialisation: take it only when your arm and eye are already sure.

objects.name: Steel Greatcleaver
objects.desc: A monstrous two-handed cleaver. A greatsword's mass with a butcher's edge and crit, devastating in the right hands, but it drinks stamina fast, so only a deep-winded slayer keeps swinging it. The apex of the high-STR cutting build.

objects.name: Steel Flail
objects.desc: A spiked steel head on a chain. Hard to aim and wild in the hand, but when it lands it lands HARD, it whips around a shield and crushes with rare, brutal luck. The mace-wielder's specialisation: blunt power turned to crit.

objects.name: Iron Rondel Dagger
objects.desc: A stiff iron spike with round guards. Made for the wrestle: it punches through a mail gap and into the joint when blades are too close to swing, fast, vicious, lucky.

objects.name: Steel Stiletto
objects.desc: A needle of hardened steel, no edge, all point. It finds the seam in any harness and slips between ribs. The assassin's tool: blink-fast, and when it goes deep it kills outright.

objects.name: Iron Estoc
objects.desc: A long, stiff, edgeless thrusting sword, half spear, half blade. It is FINESSE made steel: a keen EYE, not a strong arm, drives the point home (damage scales with Perception). Lands almost any thrust, but the constant guard and lunge are tiring. The precursor of the duelist's rapier.

objects.name: Steel Rapier
objects.desc: A slender steel duelling blade. FINESSE: its damage rides Perception, not Strength, a precise master finds the killing line where a brute would only flail. Deadly accurate and high-crit, but it drinks stamina with every parry and lunge. The high-PER one-handed duelist's masterpiece (pairs with the off-hand-free grip).

objects.name: War Bow
objects.desc: A heavy war bow with a long draw weight. Punches through leather and light mail.

objects.name: Throwing Stone
objects.desc: A fist-sized rock, hurled. Crude, short-ranged, and gone once thrown.

objects.name: Blowgun
objects.desc: A long hollowed cane that spits a slim dart on a breath of air. Barely a whisper in flight, and the dart asks for an eye or a throat to matter.

objects.name: Hunting Recurve
objects.desc: A short bow of laid wood and sinew, curved back on itself for a smooth, quiet loose. It gives up the war bow's punch for a hunter's placement.

objects.name: Sling
objects.desc: A leather cradle on two cords. Whips a stone out faster and farther than an arm alone.

objects.name: Throwing Spear
objects.desc: A light spear balanced to be thrown. Hits hard but leaves your hand.

objects.name: Crossbow
objects.desc: A stock-mounted bow drawn by a lever. Hits like a hammer; slow to span between shots.

objects.name: Blow Dart
objects.desc: A slim hardwood needle fletched with a twist of down, sized to a blowgun's bore.

objects.name: Sling Stone
objects.desc: A knapped round river stone, sized for a sling cradle. Crushes more than it cuts.

objects.name: Cast Sling Bullet
objects.desc: A biconical cast-metal bullet, the slinger's glans. Dense and fast, it drives deep where a stone would skip; the lead-shot of the ancient world.

objects.name: Flint-Tipped Arrow
objects.desc: A reed shaft fletched and tipped with a knapped flint point. Crude, but it flies and it bites.

objects.name: Bone-Tipped Arrow
objects.desc: A shaft tipped with a ground splinter of bone, a needle point that slips between fibres better than flint, but snaps on bone of its own.

objects.name: Broadhead Arrow
objects.desc: A wide, razor-edged hunting head. It opens a gaping wound that bleeds hard, murder on unarmoured flesh, but its breadth catches and turns on mail.

objects.name: Iron Bodkin Arrow
objects.desc: A narrow square-section iron bodkin, forged to one purpose: to punch through riveted mail where a broadhead would only dent it.

objects.name: Barbed War Arrow
objects.desc: An iron head with rearward barbs that lodge in the wound, it cannot be drawn back out without tearing, so it bleeds on and is rarely recovered whole.

objects.name: Iron Crossbow Bolt
objects.desc: A short, heavy iron-headed quarrel. The crossbow's stored force behind that stubby mass hits like a hammer and bores deep.

objects.name: Hardened Quarrel
objects.desc: A case-hardened pyramidal bolt head, forged and quenched to shatter plate. The siege-engineer's answer to the knight.

objects.name: Hide Quiver
objects.desc: A crude tube of stiffened green hide lashed shut at one end and slung on the back. It keeps a bundle of arrows to hand far better than groping in a sack, the first hunter's quiver. Owns the shoulders, so no pack rides with it.

objects.name: Leather Back Quiver
objects.desc: A tall sewn-leather quiver worn across the back, its mouth flared so a fletcher's reach finds a shaft without a glance. The standing archer's tool, but its bulk owns the shoulders, leaving no room for a pack.

objects.name: Stiffened War Quiver
objects.desc: A war quiver of set boar hide over an iron spine, its arrows held nock-up in a fitted spacer so a full sheaf comes to the string fast and clean. The drilled bowman's edge, and still no shoulder for a pack.

objects.name: Leather Bolt-Case
objects.desc: A stiff leather case of crossbow bolts worn at the hip. Short quarrels stack tight, so it rides the belt and leaves the back free for a proper pack, the crossbowman's quiet advantage over the archer.

objects.name: Iron-Banded Bolt-Case
objects.desc: An iron-banded hardwood bolt-case with a sprung lip that feeds quarrels one-handed while the other spans the bow. The siege-crew's belt kit, fast to feed, and the back stays free for the march pack.

objects.name: Stone-Headed Club
objects.desc: A river cobble sunk into a split branch and bound with cord. It does what weight does and nothing more, and the head works loose about as often as it lands.

objects.name: Flint Dagger
objects.desc: A long bifacial blade knapped down both faces and lashed into a split grip, longer than the flake a butcher carries. Sharper than any metal on the day it is made, and blunt or snapped by the end of the week.

objects.name: Copper Shortsword
objects.desc: A short cast blade with a riveted tang, the length of a forearm and no longer, because copper any longer than that folds. The edge goes soft after a few exchanges and the owner grinds it back at every halt.

objects.name: Copper-Headed Mace
objects.desc: A cast copper head sunk onto an ash shaft. Soft metal costs nothing here: the weight does the work, and a dented head still caves a helm.

objects.name: Copper-Socket Spear
objects.desc: The first head cast with a hollow socket, so the shaft seats inside the metal instead of being lashed alongside it. It stays true through a thrust that would have snapped a bound point.

objects.name: Copper Flat-Axe
objects.desc: A flat copper blade bound into a split elbow of yew. Heavier through the swing than any knapped head, and it bites a shield rim rather than skidding off it.

objects.name: Bronze Leaf-Sword
objects.desc: A cast blade that swells to a leaf near the point, putting the weight out where the cut lands. Sharpened along its whole length, it thrusts as readily as it hews.

objects.name: Bronze Flanged Mace
objects.desc: Cast with raised ribs down the head, so the force of a blow arrives on a narrow edge instead of spreading across a curve. Helms fold along the line it leaves.

objects.name: Bronze Socketed Spear
objects.desc: A narrow bronze head on a seasoned shaft, ground to a stiff central rib that will not fold when it meets a boss. The line weapon of every levy that can afford metal.

objects.name: Bronze Chopping Cleaver
objects.desc: A slab of cast bronze with all its mass in the last hand's width of blade. It opens a limb wide and takes the arm with it, and the arm tires fast.

objects.name: Bronze Chain Flail
objects.desc: A cast head swinging on four links of chain. The chain carries it around a raised shield and it arrives wherever it arrives, which is as much a surprise to the swinger as to the struck.

objects.name: Bronze Rapier
objects.desc: A long, narrow bronze blade riveted to a small hilt, made only to go forward. Straight on it finds the gap under a ribcage; turned aside by a hard parry it takes a set and never runs true again.

objects.name: Bronze Great-Leaf Sword
objects.desc: A long two-handed casting, broad through the belly and thin at the tang. It sweeps a wide arc and pays for the reach: bronze that length remembers every hard block as a bend.

objects.name: Bronze Greatcleaver
objects.desc: Two hands of haft behind a broad bronze chopping blade. Every swing is a commitment, and what it lands on comes apart along the cut.

objects.name: Bronze Double-Axe
objects.desc: Twin crescent blades cast around a single socket, balanced so the haft sits still in the hands. The far edge comes back on the recovery and a shield rim splits under either one.

objects.name: Bronze-Headed Maul
objects.desc: A block of cast bronze on a long two-handed shaft. It ignores what a man is wearing and settles the question with the ground he lands on.

objects.name: Bronze-Capped Staff
objects.desc: A shoulder-high ash pole with a cast ferrule at each end. It costs almost nothing, tires nobody, and rings off a skull from further away than a sword can reach.

objects.name: Iron Butcher's Cleaver
objects.desc: A butcher's tool taken to war, its spine thick and its edge ground thin. It parts a shoulder the way it parts a carcass, and the wound it leaves does not close on its own.

objects.name: Iron Ball-Flail
objects.desc: A forged iron ball on a short chain and a leather-wrapped grip. It goes over the rim of a shield and comes down behind it, and there is no guard that answers that.

objects.name: Iron Winged Spear
objects.desc: A heavy iron head with two lugs swept back below the blade. They stop the point at a hand's depth, so a charging boar or a charging man is held off the shaft instead of running up it.

objects.name: Iron Broadaxe
objects.desc: A wide crescent of iron on a shaft as long as a man's leg. Boards split, rims tear, and the thing hanging off the arm behind them stops being a shield.

objects.name: Iron Greatcleaver
objects.desc: A broad iron chopping blade set on a two-handed haft, heavy enough that the swing finishes itself. Whatever it opens keeps bleeding long after the line has moved on.

objects.name: Iron-Shod Quarterstaff
objects.desc: Seasoned ash with iron collars driven onto both ends. It answers faster than anything with an edge, and the man it keeps knocking down never gets his own swing away.

objects.name: Steel Broadaxe
objects.desc: A steel bit forge-welded into a wrought cheek, the edge hardened and the body left soft so it takes a shock without cracking. Made to be swung one-handed all day beside a shield.

objects.name: Steel Boar-Spear
objects.desc: A hardened steel head above a forged crossbar, on a shaft wrapped in cord for a wet grip. It goes through mail and then refuses to go any further, holding what it hit at arm's length.

objects.name: Steel Greataxe
objects.desc: A long-bearded steel head, the horns drawn out until the blade is nearly a half-moon. Nothing carried on an arm survives two of these, and neither does much of the arm.

objects.name: Steel Halberd
objects.desc: A spike for the thrust, an axe blade for the cut and a rear hook for the man who would rather stay upright. Three answers on one shaft, and the hook decides most fights.

objects.name: Steel-Shod Longstaff
objects.desc: A long staff bound in steel at the ends and the middle grip. It draws no blood worth speaking of and leaves whoever it works on lying down for someone else to finish.

objects.name: Rune-Etched Splitting Axe
objects.desc: Glyphs run the length of the bit and glow faintly as the head comes round. Plate parts under it like green wood.

objects.name: Rune-Ribbed Mace
objects.desc: Each flange carries a cut sigil, and the head lands harder than the arm behind it should manage. Men go down from blows that barely touched them.

objects.name: Rune-Toothed Cleaver
objects.desc: The edge is scalloped into fine teeth, each one bearing a mark no larger than a grain. What it opens will not clot while the wielder still stands.

objects.name: Steel Greatflail
objects.desc: Two hands on a long haft and a head the size of a fist, swung wide. Nothing about it is precise. It goes through a raised shield and finds whatever was behind it.

objects.name: Rune-Lashing Greatflail
objects.desc: The haft is graven the whole of its length and the head comes around faster than the swing accounts for. Braced men have been taken off their feet by the wind of it.

objects.name: Rune-Etched Arming Sword
objects.desc: A plain cruciform blade with the inscription running down the fuller, balanced a finger's width from the guard. It asks nothing of the arm that holds it and answers every part of the wrist.

objects.name: Rune-Standard Glaive
objects.desc: A glaive with the colours hung below the head, carried at the front of a line where everyone can see it. Holding it up is most of the work; the blade on top is not decoration either.

objects.name: Rune-Chained Flail
objects.desc: Every link is inscribed, and the chain keeps a truer line than chain has any business keeping. It still arrives from an angle nobody was watching.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Spear
objects.desc: A slender graven head that meets armour as though it were cloth, and shoves what it meets a pace backward. The shaft never seems to be where the enemy swings.

objects.name: Rune-Needle Rapier
objects.desc: A blade ground so fine the runes along it read as a single line. It finds the seam between two plates on the first thrust and comes back clean.

objects.name: Rune-Slotted Stiletto
objects.desc: A triangular spike with a slot cut down each face, each slot packed with ground gem. It parts riveted mail with a push and leaves a hole nobody can dress.

objects.name: Rune-Sung Greatsword
objects.desc: The fuller is filled end to end with cut verse, and the blade hums a half-tone as it travels. Whole ranks give ground rather than stand in the arc.

objects.name: Rune-Bitten Greataxe
objects.desc: A vast graven crescent that takes shields, arms and the wall behind them in one pass. It asks for a back that can carry it.

objects.name: Rune-Fanged Greatcleaver
objects.desc: A great chopping blade with a row of graven fangs along the belly. It comes away wet and whatever it touched keeps emptying.

objects.name: Rune-Weighted Warhammer
objects.desc: The head weighs more at the moment of contact than it does in the hand, and the marks cut into it are the reason. Plate caves inward and stays caved.

objects.name: Rune-Etched Halberd
objects.desc: Spike, blade and hook, every face of it written on. The hook takes a rider off a horse and the spike is already waiting where he lands.

objects.name: Rune-Banded Longstaff
objects.desc: Plain wood under bands of written alloy, and it moves faster than the eye that follows it. Nobody it works on is ever standing when the fight ends.

objects.name: Sinew-Backed Bow
objects.desc: A turned stave with dried tendon glued along its back, so the wood is pulled instead of stretched at full draw. It stores half again what the same stave managed bare.

objects.name: Horn Composite Bow
objects.desc: Horn on the belly, sinew on the back and a thin core of wood between, glued and bound and left a season to cure. Short enough to carry anywhere and it draws like a bow twice its length.

objects.name: Yew Longbow
objects.desc: A stave taller than the archer, cut where the heartwood meets the sap so the two woods fight each other at full draw. It is drawn with the back and the whole body, not the arm.

objects.name: Rune-Strung Warbow
objects.desc: A graven warbow strung with written thread that takes back some of the weight of the draw. The shaft leaves it flat and does not seem to slow.

objects.name: Composite-Prod Crossbow
objects.desc: A horn-and-sinew prod lashed across a carved stock, held by a turned bone nut and a cast pin. A week's teaching is enough, which is the whole point of it.

objects.name: Steel-Prod Arbalest
objects.desc: A steel prod no arm can bend, spanned by a windlass cranked against the stirrup. Between shots the crew is defenceless, and the shot goes through both sides of a breastplate.

objects.name: Rune-Cranked Arbalest
objects.desc: A written crank that spans a prod no windlass could, and holds it without complaint. What it looses does not stop at the first man.

objects.name: Staff-Sling
objects.desc: A sling cradle on the end of a stout pole, worked with both hands. The stone goes up and comes down steeply, which is bad news for anyone crouched behind a shield.

objects.name: Rune-Whistling Sling
objects.desc: Written cords that shriek as they come round. The shot arrives with the sound and men flinch into it.

objects.name: Bronze-Tipped Javelin
objects.desc: A light shaft weighted behind a narrow cast head, cut to a length that leaves the hand cleanly. Two or three go out before the lines meet.

objects.name: Pilum
objects.desc: A small pyramidal head on a long untempered iron shank. It punches the boards and then folds under its own weight, and the shield it is hanging from has to be thrown away.

objects.name: Francisca
objects.desc: A short throwing axe with an arched head, flung low so it skips and turns. Whichever way it lands it lands heavy, and boards are what it lands on.

objects.name: Steel Plumbata
objects.desc: A short lead-weighted dart with a steel point and stiff fletching, half a dozen clipped behind a shield. Thrown overarm at the last moment before contact.

objects.name: Rune-Marked Javelin
objects.desc: A written shaft that holds its line through wind and picks up speed on the way down. It goes through the shield and the man both.

objects.name: Cinder Rod
objects.desc: A short emberwood rod with a chip of ruby set in the head. It throws a fistful of fire and leaves the shield arm free to answer for the caster.

objects.name: Hoarfrost Rod
objects.desc: A pale rod capped with cut sapphire, cold enough to ache through a glove. What it touches goes stiff before it goes down.

objects.name: Storm Rod
objects.desc: A topaz-tipped rod that spits a thin white line rather than a bolt. It cares nothing for what the target is wearing and a great deal about how much is left in the caster.

objects.name: Copper Rod
objects.desc: A wooden rod capped in copper with a rough citrine chip bound at the tip — duller and cheaper than a cut ruby, but warm enough for a novice to draw a flicker of flame from it.

objects.name: Iron Rod
objects.desc: An iron-bound rod set with a plain cut topaz. No attunement in it, no gold — just enough of a spark to answer a caster's reach.

objects.name: Steel Rod
objects.desc: A steel-shod rod holding a plain cut sapphire. Nothing fancy binds the cold into it, but it goes through mail the same as its finer cousins.

objects.name: Emberglass Scepter
objects.desc: An attuned ruby seated in a collar of fired glass. The gout it throws hangs and burns after it lands.

objects.name: Rimeglass Scepter
objects.desc: An attuned sapphire in a frosted glass collar. The bolt goes in through mail as if the rings were not there.

objects.name: Stormglass Scepter
objects.desc: An attuned topaz behind a lens of storm glass. Armour is an invitation to it.

objects.name: Manaforge Greatstaff
objects.desc: A shaft of written alloy carrying all three cut stones at once, drawing on whichever the moment wants. It empties a caster in a handful of casts and is worth every one of them.

objects.name: Bronze-Tipped Arrow
objects.desc: A cast bronze point on a straightened shaft. Heavier than flint and it keeps its shape after it strikes, so most of a volley can be walked back and picked up.

objects.name: Steel Bodkin Arrow
objects.desc: A hardened four-sided spike, ground to a needle and left unbarbed so it drives straight on through. Made for the rings and the plate behind them.

objects.name: Steel Broadhead Arrow
objects.desc: Two hardened steel blades swept back from a sharp shoulder. It takes a horse down and it takes an unarmoured man apart, and it turns on anything riveted.

objects.name: Bronze-Headed Bolt
objects.desc: A stubby shaft with a cast bronze head and vanes of shaved horn. Short, heavy, and it does not much care about wind.

objects.name: Steel Quarrel
objects.desc: A short heavy bolt with a hardened steel head and a socket that will not split. Behind a spanned prod it goes in to the fletching.

objects.name: Fired Clay Bullet
objects.desc: A clay acorn rolled by hand and baked hard, made forty to a tray. It shatters on impact and is worth nothing afterwards, which nobody minds at that price.

objects.name: Lead Glans
objects.desc: A small almond of cast lead, half the size of a stone and twice its weight. It goes further, drops less, and buries itself where a stone would have bruised.

objects.name: Iron-Bossed Kite Shield
objects.desc: An oak kite shield with an iron boss and leather facing. Excellent defence.

objects.name: Wicker Vest
objects.desc: Green withies woven into a stiff shell and worn outermost, where it can splinter instead of a rib. It is rebuilt, never repaired.

objects.name: Cured Hide Vest
objects.desc: A sleeveless vest of ash-cured hide, stiff across the chest and laced down one side. It goes on over whatever is already being worn.

objects.name: Cured Hide Hood
objects.desc: Cured hide cut in two panels and seamed over the crown, falling past the ears and tying under the chin.

objects.name: Linen Gambeson
objects.desc: A quilted linen coat. The foundation layer for any serious warrior.

objects.name: Boarhide Jerkin
objects.desc: A sleeveless jerkin of set boar hide, laced down the flank with sinew. Boar back is the thickest hide a hunter brings home, and it turns a cut better than anything else at this age.

objects.name: Soot-Darkened Jerkin
objects.desc: A quilted jerkin of supple leather rubbed with lamp-soot until it swallows the light. Thin stuff against a blade; the work it does is not being seen.

objects.name: Leather Coif
objects.desc: A close-fitting leather hood protecting the head and neck.

objects.name: Brimmed Leather Hood
objects.desc: A soft leather hood with a low brim that cuts the glare and steadies the eye.

objects.name: Leather Vambraces
objects.desc: Stiff leather vambraces that guard the forearm from the string and free a faster draw.

objects.name: Leather Cloak
objects.desc: A long leather cloak, cut wide enough to kneel behind; its weight settles the aim for the long shot.

objects.name: Crested Bronze Helm
objects.desc: Beaten from one sheet with only a T of an opening for the eyes and mouth, and a horsehair crest riveted along the crown. Almost nothing gets through it. You will not hear a flanker and you will not see one either.

objects.name: Spangenhelm
objects.desc: Four iron plates riveted to a browband and a spanning frame, open at the face. It costs a quarter of what a raised helm does and leaves your eyes and ears where they can be used.

objects.name: Kettle Hat
objects.desc: A broad iron brim on a shallow bowl, worn by anyone who spends the day under something that might fall on them. Sheds a downward blow and a downpour alike; the brim is exactly where a sideways cut wants to be.

objects.name: Sallet
objects.desc: A tailed skull with a slit at the brow, worn with the chin covered by a separate bevor. Drop your head and the slit closes to nothing; lift it and you can see the field.

objects.name: Barbute
objects.desc: Raised from a single plate with a T-slot cut down the face, following the skull so closely there is nothing for a point to catch. What it gives up in coverage it gives back in what you can see coming.

objects.name: Cast Bronze Cervelliere
objects.desc: A plain bronze dome cast in one piece and worn over a coif. It rings like a bell when struck, and the wearer hears it from the inside.

objects.name: Stitched Leather Gauntlets
objects.desc: Padded leather gloves stitched for combat. Protects hands and wrists.

objects.name: Leather Boots
objects.desc: Ankle boots of thick hide with the fur turned inward, greased along the seams. They keep the wet out for about a season.

objects.name: Iron Mail Coif
objects.desc: A hood of riveted iron rings. Worn over a padded arming cap.

objects.name: Iron Nasal Helm
objects.desc: A formed iron helm with a nasal guard. Standard Tier 2 head armour.

objects.name: Iron Mail Hauberk
objects.desc: A knee-length coat of riveted iron rings, slit front and back to sit a horse. Two months of a smith's evenings, ring by ring.

objects.name: Iron-Plated Jack
objects.desc: Small iron plates riveted between two layers of linen, so the coat looks like cloth and turns like metal. Every rivet head shows on the outside in neat rows.

objects.name: Riveted Iron Gauntlets
objects.desc: Iron-plated gauntlets with a leather palm lining. Strong hand protection.

objects.name: Iron-Shod Boots
objects.desc: Heavy leather boots reinforced with iron plates. Brutal and protective.

objects.name: Cured Hide Skirt
objects.desc: A wrap of cured hide belted at the waist and falling to just above the knee. Below that there is nothing but shin.

objects.name: Boarhide Bracers
objects.desc: Boar hide moulded around the forearm and stitched with sinew, ridged where the shoulder plate of the animal was. Stiff enough that the wrist stops short of a full turn.

objects.name: Boarhide Greaves
objects.desc: Shaped boar hide strapped over shin and thigh. Heavy on a march, and a boar that has already been through a tusk fight has hide worth the weight.

objects.name: Cast Bronze Bracers
objects.desc: Split bronze tubes clasped around the forearms, edges rolled so they don't bite the wrist.

objects.name: Cast Bronze Greaves
objects.desc: Bronze shin-plates in the old hoplite pattern, sprung to grip the calf.

objects.name: Iron Mail Bracers
objects.desc: Iron splints riveted to leather backing, buckled from wrist to elbow.

objects.name: Iron Mail Greaves
objects.desc: Iron shin-plates over padded hose, strapped behind the calf.

objects.name: Steel Vambraces
objects.desc: Hinged steel forearm-guards that close like a clamshell and lock at the wrist.

objects.name: Steel Greaves
objects.desc: Full steel leg-plates, shin and knee-cop in one articulated piece.

objects.name: Cured Hide Boots
objects.desc: Cured hide drawn up around the foot and gathered at the ankle with a thong, the sole doubled and stitched from the inside. Shapeless until it has been walked in.

objects.name: Copper Scale Shirt
objects.desc: Hundreds of small copper scales punched and sewn onto a hide backing, each row overlapping the one below. Copper folds where iron would hold, so a hard blow leaves a dent to be hammered flat again rather than a split.

objects.name: Copper Scale Helm
objects.desc: A leather cap faced with copper scales across the crown and temples. Quick to make once the ore runs, and quick to patch when a scale tears loose.

objects.name: Copper Scale Bracers
objects.desc: Strips of copper scale sewn to leather sleeves, wrist to elbow, scales facing down so a parry slides off them.

objects.name: Copper Scale Greaves
objects.desc: Scaled leather aprons buckled over shin and thigh. Heavy on a long march, and worth carrying when the spears come in low.

objects.name: Linen Robe
objects.desc: A plain linen robe with wide sleeves and a corded belt, cut long enough to kneel in. Warm at a night desk, thin cover in a fight.

objects.name: Three-Finger Glove
objects.desc: A leather glove with three thickened fingers, cut to draw a string without stripping skin off them. The palm is left bare so the nock can still be felt.

objects.name: Arming Coif
objects.desc: A quilted cap tied under the chin, cut deep enough to sit beneath a helm without shifting. It takes the ring of a blow that the steel above it stopped.

objects.name: Arming Doublet
objects.desc: Densely quilted linen with mail voiders sewn into the armpits and inside the elbows, and waxed points laid along the shoulders and hips to tie plate to. It is the garment plate is hung from; worn alone it is a warm coat that stops a knife.

objects.name: Arming Trousers
objects.desc: Quilted hose with points at the waist, cut to take the weight of greaves without binding at the knee.

objects.name: Quilted Linen Jack
objects.desc: Thirty layers of linen stitched into narrow vertical channels and stuffed with tow. It turns a cut better than hardened leather and it drinks rain like a sponge.

objects.name: Steel Burgonet
objects.desc: A ridged steel skull with a fixed brim and hinged cheek-plates, open across the face. Cheap to raise from sheet, and a man can see and breathe in it.

objects.name: Sheet-Steel Breastplate
objects.desc: A plain breastplate beaten to a standard pattern and issued by the crate, fitted to no one chest in particular. It gaps at the arms of a broad man and rides on the hips of a small one.

objects.name: Steel Splint Bracers
objects.desc: Vertical steel splints riveted onto leather sleeves. Less proof than a hinged vambrace, and a tenth of the work to make.

objects.name: Steel Splint Greaves
objects.desc: Rows of steel splint over a leather backing, laced up the calf. A footman's leg armour, turned out by the hundred.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Cuirass
objects.desc: Alloy plate cut through with graven lines that carry the harness's weight down into the hips instead of hanging it off the shoulders. Unbuckled, it stands up on its own.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Helm
objects.desc: A closed helm whose graven bands hold the plate rigid at half the thickness. The sight is a single slit and the whole world narrows into it.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Vambraces
objects.desc: Graven forearm-plates that close without a hinge and stay shut through a blow.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Greaves
objects.desc: Alloy leg-plates whose graven lines take the shock of a footfall out of the knee.

objects.name: Rune-Stitched Lamellar
objects.desc: Small alloy plates laced edge to edge with enchanted thread that will not fray or stretch. The coat moves like cloth and stops a blow like plate.

objects.name: Rune-Stitched Coif
objects.desc: A hood of laced alloy scales on enchanted thread, closing under the chin. It lies flat enough to take a helm over the top.

objects.name: Rune-Woven Robe
objects.desc: Silk shot through with enchanted thread in a close spiral. The weave goes rigid the instant something strikes it and hangs soft again after.

objects.name: Rune-Woven Hood
objects.desc: A deep silk hood woven with the same spiral thread. It shrugs off cold and turns a glancing edge.

objects.name: Jackal-Leather Coif
objects.desc: Cut in four panels and seamed over the crown, with a throat flap that laces under the jaw. Cut from thin, dust-coloured jackal hide. It creases silently and weighs almost nothing on a long stalk.

objects.name: Jackal-Leather Jerkin
objects.desc: Sleeveless, laced down the flank so it can be pulled on over a wet shirt. Cut from thin, dust-coloured jackal hide. It creases silently and weighs almost nothing on a long stalk.

objects.name: Jackal-Leather Bracers
objects.desc: Wrapped from wrist to elbow and pulled tight with a thong through paired slits. Cut from thin, dust-coloured jackal hide. It creases silently and weighs almost nothing on a long stalk.

objects.name: Jackal-Leather Gloves
objects.desc: Cut with a separate thumb and a doubled palm, the seams turned inward. Cut from thin, dust-coloured jackal hide. It creases silently and weighs almost nothing on a long stalk.

objects.name: Jackal-Leather Greaves
objects.desc: Bound over shin and thigh, with the knee left open so a stride is not shortened. Cut from thin, dust-coloured jackal hide. It creases silently and weighs almost nothing on a long stalk.

objects.name: Jackal-Leather Boots
objects.desc: Ankle-high, seams greased, the sole doubled where a heel wears through first. Cut from thin, dust-coloured jackal hide. It creases silently and weighs almost nothing on a long stalk.

objects.name: Boarhide Helm
objects.desc: Cut in four panels and seamed over the crown, with a throat flap that laces under the jaw. Cut from stiff boar hide, thickest over the shoulders. It sets into whatever curve it was shaped in and never softens again.

objects.name: Boarhide Gloves
objects.desc: Cut with a separate thumb and a doubled palm, the seams turned inward. Cut from stiff boar hide, thickest over the shoulders. It sets into whatever curve it was shaped in and never softens again.

objects.name: Boarhide Boots
objects.desc: Ankle-high, seams greased, the sole doubled where a heel wears through first. Cut from stiff boar hide, thickest over the shoulders. It sets into whatever curve it was shaped in and never softens again.

objects.name: Buckskin Jerkin
objects.desc: Sleeveless, laced down the flank so it can be pulled on over a wet shirt. Cut from soft buckskin, rubbed until it falls in easy folds. It takes a dye well and makes no sound against a bowstring.

objects.name: Buckskin Boots
objects.desc: Ankle-high, seams greased, the sole doubled where a heel wears through first. Cut from soft buckskin, rubbed until it falls in easy folds. It takes a dye well and makes no sound against a bowstring.

objects.desc: Cut in four panels and seamed over the crown, with a throat flap that laces under the jaw. Plain linen work, matched to the rest of the kit.

objects.name: Linen Boots

objects.desc: Wrapped from wrist to elbow and pulled tight with a thong through paired slits. Riveted Iron work, matched to the rest of the kit.

objects.name: Riveted Iron Greaves
objects.desc: Bound over shin and thigh, with the knee left open so a stride is not shortened. Riveted Iron work, matched to the rest of the kit.

objects.desc: Cut in four panels and seamed over the crown, with a throat flap that laces under the jaw. Quilted Linen work, matched to the rest of the kit.

objects.name: Quilted Linen Gloves
objects.desc: Cut with a separate thumb and a doubled palm, the seams turned inward. Quilted Linen work, matched to the rest of the kit.

objects.name: Sabretooth-Leather Coif
objects.desc: Cut in four panels and seamed over the crown, with a throat flap that laces under the jaw. Cut from dense sabretooth hide, scarred across the flank. The cat that wore it had been fighting for years, and the hide shows every one.

objects.desc: Sleeveless, laced down the flank so it can be pulled on over a wet shirt. Cut from dense sabretooth hide, scarred across the flank. The cat that wore it had been fighting for years, and the hide shows every one.

objects.name: Sinew
objects.desc: Tough dried animal tendon. Used for binding, bowstrings, and stitching.

objects.name: Flax Fiber
objects.desc: Processed flax stalks ready for spinning into linen thread.

objects.name: Spider Silk Thread
objects.desc: Drawn off a weaver's hoard and doubled on the wheel. Thinner than linen thread and it will not part under a load that snaps sinew.

objects.name: Spun Thread
objects.desc: Strong spun thread, walked off a spinning wheel from flax or wool. Supersedes raw cordage and rope as binding from the bronze age on, sews, lashes and strings without the bulk.

objects.name: Linen Cloth
objects.desc: Woven linen fabric. A basic textile for clothing and bandaging.

objects.name: Heartwood Log
objects.desc: Timber from an ancient elder grove, grain coiled like a slow heartbeat. Prized for staves and prestige work.

objects.name: Moonwood Log
objects.desc: Pale, near-weightless timber from a moonlit silver-birch grove. Sings under a bowyer's knife.

objects.name: Witchwood Log
objects.desc: Dark, close-grained timber from the deep old-growth, the wood itself holding a charge that lingers after the axe. A haft cut from it does not want to let a spell go.

objects.name: Soulwood Heart
objects.desc: The dense golden core of a tree older than any living memory, cut from the heart of an ancient stand. It takes an edge and a name, and keeps both.

objects.name: Frostheart Timber
objects.desc: Pine cut from the cold heart of the mountains, the resin gone to a blue rime that never quite thaws. A cold breath rises off the fresh-cut end.

objects.name: Bonewood
objects.desc: Pale, near-weightless timber from a snag long dead on its feet. Thirsty stuff — it drinks in oil or venom and holds it deep in the grain.

objects.name: Ironwood Log
objects.desc: Black, iron-dense timber from a deep darkwood grove. Unyielding, hafts, shafts, and shields.

objects.name: Emberwood Log
objects.desc: Warm-to-the-touch timber from a sun-scorched grove, embers glowing in the grain. For fire foci and braziers.

objects.name: Bloodroot
objects.desc: A red taproot that weeps a warm sap the colour of blood when the knife goes in. The old herb-wives pressed it for the failing and the fevered.

objects.name: Dreamleaf
objects.desc: Silver-backed leaves that fold shut at a passing footstep. Steeped, they carry a still, dreamless quiet into a troubled mind.

objects.name: Mandrake
objects.desc: A forked root shaped like a small man, said to scream as it leaves the earth. A base for the deepest draughts, and a thing handled with care.

objects.name: Emberbloom
objects.desc: A coal-red flower that smoulders faintly as the light fails, warm to the cupped hand. It carries the memory of a heat that does not burn.

objects.name: Glowcap
objects.desc: A pale fungus that keeps a cold blue light long after it is picked, enough to read a path by. It never seems to gutter or dim.

objects.name: Nightshade Bolete
objects.desc: Purple-gilled and swollen, weeping a single black bead at the stem. Everything about it warns the hand away, which is exactly why some hands reach for it.

objects.name: Witch's Morel
objects.desc: A honeycombed cap that never seems quite the same shape twice. The enchanters prize it as a binder; the unwary who eat it see things that are not there.

objects.name: Spore of Madness
objects.desc: A grey puffball that bursts at a touch into a slow drift of motes. Breathe them and the world tilts; distilled with care, they set the blood roaring.

objects.name: Mana Crystal
objects.desc: A clear violet crystal grown deep in the roots of the mountains, humming faintly against the palm. Ground down, it yields a purer dust than any cut gem.

objects.name: Star Shard
objects.desc: A sliver of something that fell burning from the sky and cooled in the rock around it. It catches a light that is not in the room.

objects.name: Rune-Etched Pick
objects.desc: A magic-alloy head cut through with binding glyphs that hold its edge against stone which turns steel. There is rock in the deep dark that nothing else will mark.

objects.name: Voidshard
objects.desc: A shard of black glass that drinks the light around its edges and gives a cold nothing back. Power sits in it, and a price sits beside the power.

objects.name: Heartwood Plank
objects.desc: Heartwood dressed into board, coiled grain that holds an enchantment like a vessel. The frame of runed work.

objects.name: Moonwood Plank
objects.desc: Pale, near-weightless board from a moonlit grove. Takes silver inlay and lunar runes cleanly.

objects.name: Ironwood Plank
objects.desc: Black, iron-dense board, near unbreakable. The structural runed timber for anything that must bear weight or ward.

objects.name: Emberwood Plank
objects.desc: Warm board with embers in the grain. Used where fire foci and braziers need a frame that won't char.

objects.name: Ruby
objects.desc: A cut-grade gemstone. Polished and sold, or set into fine (non-magical) jewellery.

objects.name: Infused Ruby
objects.desc: A ruby threaded with raw mana. Attuned and set, it lends the wearer might.

objects.name: Cut Ruby
objects.desc: A polished ruby, a valuable trade good and prestige adornment.

objects.name: Attuned Ruby
objects.desc: A ruby cut and attuned at the lapidary. Set into a ring or amulet, it grants Might.

objects.name: Tooth Necklace
objects.desc: Fangs drilled and strung on a thong, one for each beast that nearly won. The oldest way of saying who you are without speaking.

objects.name: Bone Circlet
objects.desc: A band of scraped bone, carved with whatever the carver's people carve. Worn by whoever the rest have decided to listen to.

objects.name: Bronze Torc
objects.desc: A heavy twisted collar with terminals cast in the shape of animal heads, sprung open just enough to force around a throat. It is not taken off, and it is not given away.

objects.name: Bronze Arm-Ring
objects.desc: A spiral of cast bronze worn high on the arm. Given by a chief to someone who did something worth paying for, and cut into pieces when the payment has to be made in metal.

objects.name: Iron Signet Ring
objects.desc: A flat bezel cut in reverse, so that pressed into wax it leaves a mark nobody else can make. The first jewellery that is also a document.

objects.name: Silver Pendant
objects.desc: Cupelled silver beaten thin and hung on a fine chain. Worth a season's work and light enough to forget you are wearing it.

objects.name: Filigree Diadem
objects.desc: Drawn silver wire soldered into a lattice so fine it seems to have grown rather than been made. The work of one person for one winter.

objects.name: Gold Chain of Office
objects.desc: Interlocking links each the weight of a coin, worn across the shoulders by whoever currently answers for the colony. It is handed on, not inherited.

objects.name: Ruby Ring
objects.desc: A gold ring set with an attuned ruby. Grants Might while worn.

objects.name: Ruby Amulet
objects.desc: A gold amulet set with a large attuned ruby. Grants Might while worn (neck slot, stacks with a ring).
