objects.name: Scholar's Circlet
objects.desc: A slender silver circlet set with an attuned sapphire. Grants Insight while worn, but a circlet is no helm, so the head goes unarmoured.

objects.name: Champion's Crown
objects.desc: A gold war-crown set with an attuned ruby and topaz. Grants both Might and Quickness, a warrior's regalia worn in place of a helm.

objects.name: Sovereign's Crown
objects.desc: A high gold crown set with an attuned citrine and amethyst. Grants Charm and Keen Senses, the regalia of a ruler, not a soldier.

objects.name: Warden's Circlet
objects.desc: A gold circlet set with an attuned emerald and moonstone. Grants Grace and Fortitude, magic poise and endurance standing in for a steel helm.

objects.name: Gold Torc
objects.desc: A heavy twisted-gold torc seated with an attuned emerald. Grants Fortitude while worn (neck slot).

objects.name: Champion's Torc
objects.desc: A gold torc set with an attuned ruby and emerald. Grants Might and Vigor, the front-line fighter's neck-piece.

objects.name: Wayfarer's Pendant
objects.desc: A silver pendant set with an attuned topaz and moonstone. Grants Quickness and Moonlit, the scout's and traveller's charm.

objects.name: Sage's Pendant
objects.desc: A gold pendant set with an attuned sapphire and citrine. Grants Insight and Charm, the counsellor's and crafter's piece.

objects.name: Ember Staff
objects.desc: An emberwood staff tipped with a cut ruby. Looses a gout of flame, its power rides the wielder's wits, not their arm. Drinks stamina with every cast.

objects.name: Pyre Staff
objects.desc: An emberwood staff bound at the Attunement Altar with an attuned ruby and gold. The flame comes hotter, farther and cheaper, and its heat lends the bearer strength while held.

objects.name: Frost Staff
objects.desc: A moonwood staff seated with a cut sapphire. Hurls a lance of biting cold, slower to bite than flame, but it slips past armour.

objects.name: Rime Staff
objects.desc: A moonwood staff bound with an attuned sapphire and gold. Its cold reaches farther and pierces deeper, and it sharpens the bearer's mind while held.

objects.name: Spark Staff
objects.desc: A heartwood staff crowned with a cut topaz. Snaps a bolt of lightning that all but ignores armour, but it is the hungriest of the staves for stamina.

objects.name: Tempest Staff
objects.desc: A heartwood staff bound with an attuned topaz and gold. Its bolt strikes farther and harder through any plate, and quickens the bearer's hand while held.

objects.name: Cart Wheel
objects.desc: A spoked wooden wheel banded with an iron rim. The heart of every barrow and cart.

objects.name: Wheelbarrow
objects.desc: A single-wheeled barrow. Pushed two-handed, no room for a weapon, but carries far more than a pawn's own back. Wants cleared ground.

objects.name: Handcart
objects.desc: A two-wheeled handcart. The first real hauler, a big carry budget, but the heavier it's loaded the slower the pawn pushing it. Both hands on the shafts: no fighting.

objects.name: Barren Dirt
objects.desc: A clod of plain, infertile earth. Filler, nothing much grows in it without improvement.

objects.name: Poor Soil
objects.desc: Thin topsoil with a little life in it. Grows hardy crops, slowly.

objects.name: Loam
objects.desc: Rich, crumbly soil. Good tilth, most crops thrive in it.

objects.name: Rich Soil
objects.desc: Dark, humus-laden earth from a deep-grass stand. Most crops flourish in it.

objects.name: Terra Preta
objects.desc: Black, charcoal-dark earth, the most fertile soil there is. Even prize crops flourish.

objects.name: Compost
objects.desc: Rotted scraps and hay broken down into dark, nutrient-rich humus. Raw compost, refine it into fertiliser to build proper soil.

objects.name: Fertiliser
objects.desc: Compost concentrated and aged into a potent soil amendment. Worked into earth with clay and dirt, it builds loam, rich soil, even terra preta.

objects.name: Grain Seed
objects.desc: A handful of cereal seed, wheat or barley. Sow it on tilled soil to grow grain.

objects.name: Cabbage Seed
objects.desc: Fine cabbage seed. Sow on tilled soil to grow a bed of leafy heads.

objects.name: Turnip Seed
objects.desc: Turnip seed. Quick, hardy roots, a dependable cold-weather crop.

objects.name: Rye Seed
objects.desc: Rye grain for sowing. The hardiest of the cereals, it germinates in near-frozen soil, so it carries the first spring planting.

objects.name: Kale Seed
objects.desc: Fine kale seed. A frost-hardy leaf, sow it early, as the cold only sweetens the heads.

objects.name: Radish Seed
objects.desc: Radish seed. The fastest root in the garden and tolerant of cold, a few weeks from sowing to the first pull.

objects.name: Onion Seed
objects.desc: Onion seed. Sow for pungent bulbs that store braided through winter.

objects.name: Bean Seed
objects.desc: Dried seed beans. Hardy, protein-rich, and they fix the soil they grow in.

objects.name: Pea Seed
objects.desc: Seed peas. Climbing pods for a thick, storable pottage.

objects.name: Fibre Seed
objects.desc: Flax and hemp seed. Grows fibrous stalks for cordage and cloth, wants damp, decent soil.

objects.name: Berry Seed
objects.desc: Berry cuttings. Sow a perennial patch that fruits year on year.

objects.name: Apple Pips
objects.desc: Apple pips. Slow to bear, but an orchard fruits for a lifetime.

objects.name: Grape Cuttings
objects.desc: Grapevine cuttings. Trained on a trellis, they bear fruit for wine.

objects.name: Thyme Seed
objects.desc: Thyme seed. A hardy perennial herb, flavour for the pot, simples for the sick.

objects.name: Mint Seed
objects.desc: Mint seed. Spreads fast into a fragrant perennial bed.

objects.name: Prize Seed
objects.desc: Seed for a demanding prize crop, pumpkin, grapevine. Only flourishes in terra preta.

objects.name: Wheat
objects.desc: Cultivated wheat grain. Raw it's gritty, hard-to-digest filler; milled to flour and baked it becomes bread (or malted for ale).

objects.name: Cabbage
objects.desc: A dense leafy head from the garden bed. Boils down into the pot; keeps a while in the cold.

objects.name: Turnip
objects.desc: A pale earthy root. Plain fare, but it stores through winter in a clamp.

objects.name: Rye
objects.desc: Cultivated rye grain. Gritty eaten raw; milled to flour it bakes into a dark, keeping loaf, the bread of cold lands.

objects.name: Kale
objects.desc: Tough, ruffled leaves that shrug off frost. Bitter raw; the cold and the pot both mellow it.

objects.name: Radish
objects.desc: A small, peppery root pulled barely a month after sowing. The first fresh bite of the season.

objects.name: Onion
objects.desc: A pungent bulb. Sharp raw, sweet in the pot, and it keeps for months braided up.

objects.name: Beans
objects.desc: Dried beans from the rows. Protein-rich, slow-cooking, and they store for an age.

objects.name: Peas
objects.desc: Dried peas, shelled from the pod. The backbone of a thick pease pottage.

objects.name: Apple
objects.desc: Crisp orchard fruit. Eaten fresh, stored in straw, or pressed for cider.

objects.name: Grapes
objects.desc: Sweet vine fruit in heavy bunches. Eaten fresh or trodden for wine.

objects.name: Sugar Cane
objects.desc: Thick, fibrous canes that grow in wet ground. Sweet to chew, but the sugar only comes free once the stalks are crushed and the juice boiled down.

objects.name: Sugar
objects.desc: Coarse pale crystals boiled down from cane juice. It keeps for a long time and feeds a strong ferment far better than plain fruit.

objects.name: Thyme
objects.desc: Fragrant cultivated thyme. A pinch lifts a stew; a poultice of it eases the sick.

objects.name: Mint
objects.desc: Cool cultivated mint. Brewed into a settling tea or strewn to sweeten a room.

objects.name: Pumpkin
objects.desc: A fat prize gourd grown only in terra preta. Hearty cooking, and a grower's pride.

objects.name: Flour
objects.desc: Grain ground fine on a quern. The base of bread, pies and pastry, not eaten raw.

objects.name: Bread
objects.desc: A dense risen loaf baked in the oven. The staff of life, filling, and it travels.

objects.name: Simple Sandwich
objects.desc: A cut loaf with something laid between the halves. Eaten standing up, on the way to somewhere else.

objects.name: Hearty Sandwich
objects.desc: Bread packed with two fillings and pressed flat enough to carry. What you take when the work is a long walk away.

objects.name: Game Pie
objects.desc: Cured and smoked meat baked under a standing crust. Built to be carried and cut cold, days after it left the oven.

objects.name: Honey Tart
objects.desc: A shallow crust filled with honey and fruit and baked until the top catches. Sweet enough to be worth the honey.

objects.name: Pie
objects.desc: A single filling baked into a pastry crust. Plain, but a proper baked meal.

objects.name: Fine Pie
objects.desc: Two fillings baked into a pastry crust. A hot, hearty meal in the hand.

objects.name: Hearty Pie
objects.desc: A deep three-filling pie under a thick golden crust. A feast that steels the body for the day.

objects.name: Honey
objects.desc: Sweet golden honey. Eaten as a treat and kept indefinitely. (Beekeeping, ENTITIES D.)

objects.name: Malt
objects.desc: Grain steeped, sprouted and kilned in the fermenter, the sugary base that ferments into ale.

objects.name: Ale
objects.desc: Cloudy malt ale, mashed and fermented in the cask. Lifts the spirits, and goes to the head.

objects.name: Herbal Tea
objects.desc: Fragrant herbs steeped in hot water. Calms the body and eases small aches, a brew for the mending.

objects.name: Table Wine
objects.desc: Fruit pressed and fermented to a deep, heady wine. A finer drink, and a stronger one.

objects.name: Birch Sap Wine
objects.desc: Spring sap left in a covered crock until it works on its own. Thin, faintly sweet and barely strong enough to notice, which is all anyone expected of it.

objects.name: Mead
objects.desc: Honey and water left to work through a whole summer. Sweet, heavy and strong enough that it was poured for oaths rather than for thirst.

objects.name: Barley Beer
objects.desc: Malted grain mashed, soured and drunk cloudy within the week. Thick enough to be counted as food by the people drinking it, and safer than the well.

objects.name: Grape Wine
objects.desc: Pressed, left on its skins, then racked off the lees into a bunged cask. It travels, it keeps, and it is the first thing this colony makes that another kingdom will want.

objects.name: Hopped Ale
objects.desc: The same mash, bittered with hops that keep it drinkable for months instead of days. The invention that let beer be brewed somewhere other than where it was drunk.

objects.name: Apple Brandy
objects.desc: Cider run through the still twice and rested in oak until it stops biting. Small, strong and worth more by weight than anything else the orchard produces.

objects.name: Grain Whisky
objects.desc: Malt dried over peat smoke, distilled, and left in a charred cask for years while it turns from raw spirit into something worth waiting for.

objects.name: Fortified Wine
objects.desc: Wine arrested mid-ferment with a measure of spirit, leaving it sweet and strong enough to cross an ocean without turning. Made to be shipped, not to be drunk at home.

objects.name: Cider
objects.desc: Pressed apples left to work in the cask until they turn sharp and bright. Keeps through winter and warms a cold night.

objects.name: Tree Resin
objects.desc: Sticky sap tapped from conifers. The earliest glue, seals buckets, hafts heads, and binds bow nocks.

objects.name: Bone Meal
objects.desc: Bone ground to a coarse powder. Boils into glue, or feeds the soil as fertiliser.

objects.name: Bone Glue
objects.desc: Strong glue boiled down from bone meal. A craftable binder that beats wild resin, no resinous grove needed.

objects.name: Hide Glue
objects.desc: Glue rendered from hide scraps and trimmings. Interchangeable with bone glue, a sink for tanning offcuts.

objects.name: Basket
objects.desc: Green withies bent round a rim and woven tight. Set it down and it holds a load of dry goods; it will not hold a drop of water.

objects.name: Bin
objects.desc: A deep plank box on a square base, joined and pegged. Takes a great deal and stacks in a corner without falling over.

objects.name: Crate
objects.desc: Slatted boards nailed into an open box. Lighter than a bin and quicker to knock together, and the gaps let a load breathe.

objects.name: Bucket
objects.desc: Resin-sealed plank-staved bucket. Carry water, or set it down and load it with brine to tan hides.

objects.name: Barrel
objects.desc: Big plank-staved cask. Set it down to steep tanning brine or ferment a brew over days.

objects.name: Tanning Brine
objects.desc: Bark-tannin pickle, salt, ash-lye and water steeped for days. The soak liquor a tanning bucket burns through to turn cured hide into leather.

objects.name: Beast Brine
objects.desc: A fierce double-strength tannin liquor of oak-gall and hardwood ash. Hot enough to bite into thick beast hide, ordinary brine can't.

objects.name: Aurochs Meat
objects.desc: Heavy slabs of wild-ox beef. Feeds a hall.

objects.name: Mammoth Meat
objects.desc: Dense, fatty proboscidean meat. One tusk-beast feeds a colony through winter.

objects.name: Owlbear Meat
objects.desc: Rank, stringy meat off a fearsome beast. Edible, just.

objects.name: Sabretooth Meat
objects.desc: Lean great-cat meat. Gamey and tough, but plentiful.

objects.name: Crocodile Meat
objects.desc: Pale, firm reptile tail-meat. Mild once cooked through.

objects.name: Hippogriff Meat
objects.desc: Half-fowl, half-horse, rich dark meat with a poultry edge.

objects.name: Fowl Meat
objects.desc: Wild-bird meat off a hoarfowl or the like. Quick and lean.

objects.name: Worg Meat
objects.desc: Coarse meat off a great wolf-beast. Tough, gamey, filling.

objects.name: Ivory
objects.desc: A mammoth tusk's dense ivory. Prestige carving, inlay, and fine hafts.

objects.name: Huge Bones
objects.desc: Colossal load-bearing bones from a mammoth or great beast. Heavy bone armour and structural carving.

objects.name: Feathers
objects.desc: Large flight feathers off a hippogriff or fowl. Fletching, stuffing, and showy trim.

objects.name: Aurochs Hide
objects.desc: A vast, heavy wild-ox hide. Cures into the toughest common leather.

objects.name: Worg Hide
objects.desc: Coarse, dense pelt of a great wolf-beast. Sturdy leather and warm cloaks.

objects.name: Owlbear Pelt
objects.desc: A dense, matted pelt, fur over a thick beast hide. Beast-grade leather backing.

objects.name: Sabretooth Pelt
objects.desc: A great-cat's dense striped pelt. Beast-grade hide, prized for armour and prestige.

objects.name: Mammoth Fur-Hide
objects.desc: Immense shaggy fur-hide. The thickest beast leather there is, and the warmest.

objects.name: Scaled Crocodile Hide
objects.desc: Armoured reptilian hide, ridged with bony scutes. Hardens into scale plate.

objects.name: Feathered Hide
objects.desc: Half-feathered, half-hide pelt of a hippogriff. Light beast-grade armour backing.

objects.name: Scale Plate
objects.desc: Hardened crocodile scutes laid like overlapping plates. Natural scale armour.

objects.name: Coney Wool
objects.desc: Downy wool combed from a rabbit's belly. Fine and very warm, though one coney gives barely a handful.

objects.name: Goat Wool
objects.desc: Coarse goat fleece with a little sheen. The everyday wool, good for cloth and plain bedding.

objects.name: Sheep Fleece
objects.desc: A full sheep's fleece. The staple wool, plentiful and easy to spin, sheared from a living flock.

objects.name: Ox Wool
objects.desc: Matted undercoat pulled in fistfuls from an aurochs. Coarse and heavy, but it traps heat like nothing else, made for blankets and padding.

objects.name: Mammoth Wool
objects.desc: Long, fine wool from beneath a mammoth's guard hair. The warmest and softest there is, and the hardest won.

objects.name: Woolcloth
objects.desc: Woven wool cloth. Furnishings, bedding, and prestige hangings.

objects.name: Cotton Seed
objects.desc: Fuzzy cotton seed. Sown in warm, well-watered ground for a fibre crop.

objects.name: Cotton
objects.desc: Ginned cotton fibre, soft, light and plentiful. Spun into thread, woven into cloth, or packed by the sackful as soft stuffing.

objects.name: Cotton Cloth
objects.desc: Light woven cotton, breathable everyday cloth for clothes, sheets and upholstery.

objects.name: Raw Silk
objects.desc: Lustrous raw silk reeled from a thornwood spider's glands. Reels and weaves into the finest cloth there is.

objects.name: Silk Cloth
objects.desc: Shimmering woven silk, light, strong and prized. The cloth of robes, mage vestments and the richest hangings.

objects.name: Stuffed Cushion
objects.desc: A cloth cushion packed firm with a heap of feathers or cotton down. The soft heart of every padded chair, couch and feather bed.

objects.name: Wool Cloak
objects.desc: A heavy woollen travelling cloak. Sheds rain and turns the cold on a long road.

objects.name: Arcane Robe
objects.desc: Silk laid down in one unbroken bolt and sewn with gem dust along every seam. It weighs nothing across the shoulders and the sigils drink what is thrown at them.

objects.name: Quicklime
objects.desc: Limestone burned in the kiln to caustic lime. The binder in mortar and concrete.

objects.name: Mortar
objects.desc: Lime, sand and water worked to a paste. Beds and binds dressed stone blocks into a lasting wall.

objects.name: Crushed Stone
objects.desc: Rock hammered to gravel. Pozzolanic aggregate for concrete, and the bed for roads.

objects.name: Concrete
objects.desc: Roman-style mix of quicklime and crushed stone. Sets hard as rock, the strongest mundane masonry.

objects.name: Rebar
objects.desc: Iron bar drawn into ribbed rod. Cast into concrete, it carries the load no stone can.

objects.name: Gem Dust
objects.desc: Mana-dust ground from an infused gem. The shared currency of every magic age, walls, infused stations, binders, potions, defences and reforging all draw on it.

objects.name: Runed Concrete
objects.desc: Concrete kneaded with gem-dust until the runes set glowing in the cure. Walls of it shrug off blade, weather and spell alike.

objects.name: Iron Wire
objects.desc: Iron bar drawn through a plate into fine wire. Coiled and cut, it becomes mail rings.

objects.name: Iron Ring-Bundle
objects.desc: A hank of some three hundred rings, wound off the wire and cut, each one still open and waiting to be riveted shut. A coif swallows ten of these and a hauberk four times that.

objects.name: Croc-Scale Cuirass
objects.desc: Bony scutes cut from a bog lurker and sewn onto a leather backing, each scale overlapping the one below. They keep the ridged grain of the animal that grew them.

objects.name: Steel Plate Cuirass
objects.desc: A fitted steel breast-and-back plate. The pinnacle of mundane body armour, turns most blows outright.

objects.name: Steel Great Helm
objects.desc: A heavy enclosed steel helm. Maximum head protection, at the price of a narrowed view.

objects.name: Layered Boarhide Plate
objects.desc: Set boar hide built up in overlapping layers and stitched through, the way a shield is built up from planks. As proof as iron against a cut, and it will not rust in the rain.

objects.name: Bone-Plated Cuirass
objects.desc: Great beast-bone plates lashed over a leather coat. Heavy, savage, and a closing of the butchery loop.

objects.name: Horned Helm
objects.desc: A bone-and-horn helm crowned with a beast's horns. Fearsome, and a peak-tier head guard.

objects.name: Ceremonial Plate
objects.desc: Gilt-and-engraved parade armour. All show and little guard, worn to command, not to fight.

objects.name: Silk Robe
objects.desc: Spider silk woven fine and hung loose from the shoulders. It slides off a glancing edge and costs the wearer nothing to walk in all day.

objects.name: Regal Robes
objects.desc: Fine woolcloth robes, dyed and trimmed for a leader's court. Negligible armour, immense bearing.

objects.name: Clay Alembic
objects.desc: A fired-clay still with a long condensing neck. The heart of the alchemy lab, distils tinctures, brines and spirits.

objects.name: Phial
objects.desc: Blown-glass flasks and phials melted from sand. Holds reagents, and bottles a finished potion.

objects.name: Unfired Jug
objects.desc: Thrown on the wheel and left leather-hard. It holds its shape and nothing else — water would soften it back to mud. It wants the kiln.

objects.name: Unfired Flask
objects.desc: A small thrown body, still damp enough to take a thumbprint. Fired it will carry a day's water; unfired it will not carry anything.

objects.name: Jug
objects.desc: A wheel-thrown, fired clay jug. The first proper vessel for oil, water and reagents, keeps stored goods sealed and a little fresher.

objects.name: Porcelain Clay
objects.desc: Fine white levigated clay, washed of grit. Fires to translucent porcelain, the raw stock of the finest ceramics.

objects.name: Porcelain Jar
objects.desc: Hard, glassy white porcelain, the finest reagent vessels there are. The top of the ceramic line; seals and preserves better than any clay.

objects.name: Tannin Concentrate
objects.desc: Bark boiled down to a strong tannin concentrate. Brews a faster, finer tanning brine.

objects.name: Dye
objects.desc: Boiled-down plant and berry colour. Stains cloth and leather for prestige goods.

objects.name: Soap
objects.desc: Fat boiled with ash-lye into a hard bar. A wash with this strips the grease the river only moves around, and the grime stays off for a day.

objects.name: Potion of Might
objects.desc: A red draught that floods the limbs with strength. Grants Might for a time once drunk.

objects.name: Draught of Vigor
objects.desc: A green tonic that banishes fatigue and steadies the wind. Grants Vigor for a time.

objects.name: Elixir of Grace
objects.desc: A clear silver elixir that quickens the step and the eye. Grants Grace for a time, offsets the load of heavy armour.

objects.name: Tonic of Fortitude
objects.desc: A dark, bitter tonic that hardens flesh against harm. Grants Fortitude for a time.

objects.name: Magic-Alloy Bar
objects.desc: Steel re-smelted with gem-dust in a runic crucible. Light, keen, and faintly aglow, the metal of mythic gear.

objects.name: Enchant-Thread
objects.desc: Fine wool spun through with gem-dust on a runic loom. Woven into prestige cloth and the linings of enchanted gear.

objects.name: Runed Block
objects.desc: A dressed block cut with gem-dust glyphs at the glyph-cutter's banker. The stone of the magic wall age.

objects.name: Tanglefoot Coating
objects.desc: A stringy amber gum boiled from pine resin and fat, daubed thick along an edge. Where it catches, it drags at sinew and gums a leg to slowness.

objects.name: Greater Tanglefoot Coating
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the tanglefoot coating, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Tanglefoot Coating
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the tanglefoot coating, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Dread Coating
objects.desc: A grey unguent of mandrake and madness-spore that smells of an open grave. The wound it rides carries a wave of unreasoning fear into the blood.

objects.name: Greater Dread Coating
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the dread coating, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Dread Coating
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the dread coating, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Farsight Tonic
objects.desc: A pale blue infusion of glowcap that pricks the senses awake. The world sharpens at its edges and little escapes the eye.

objects.name: Greater Farsight Tonic
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the farsight tonic, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Farsight Tonic
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the farsight tonic, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Antivenin Tonic
objects.desc: A bitter charcoal draught that scours the gut. It settles a churning stomach and draws the sickness out.

objects.name: Greater Antivenin Tonic
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the antivenin tonic, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Antivenin Tonic
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the antivenin tonic, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Restful Tonic
objects.desc: A sweet cordial of dreamleaf steeped with plenty of pressed berries. It unknots a tired body and lifts a low head.

objects.name: Greater Restful Tonic
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the restful tonic, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Grand Restful Tonic
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the restful tonic, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Honing Oil
objects.desc: A fine grit of river sand worked into rendered fat, rubbed the length of a blade. It draws a wicked edge that bites deep and leaves a wound slow to close.

objects.name: Keen-Edge Oil
objects.desc: A more potent, longer-lasting preparation of the honing oil, drawn off at the lab with finer reagents.

objects.name: Razor's Grace
objects.desc: A masterfully refined, powerful preparation of the honing oil, drawn off at the apothecary with finer reagents.

objects.name: Fermented Mash
objects.desc: A sour, bubbling porridge of grain and raw sugar left to work in the dark. Not fit to eat, but the beginning of a strong spirit.

objects.name: Distilled Spirit
objects.desc: A clear, biting liquor drawn off the still and filtered through charcoal. It carries an alchemist's essences far better than water or wine.

objects.name: Sackcloth Hood
objects.desc: A hood of coarse sacking, seamed up the back and pulled tight with a drawstring. It keeps the sun and the rain off and stops nothing else.

objects.name: Sackcloth Tunic
objects.desc: A shapeless tunic of coarse fibre that hangs to mid-thigh, belted with a length of cord. It is the first thing anyone here wore that was not an animal.

objects.name: Sackcloth Mitts
objects.desc: Bag-cut mitts with a separate thumb, stitched from offcuts. Warm, clumsy, and always fraying.

objects.name: Sackcloth Foot-Wraps
objects.desc: Long strips of coarse cloth wound over the foot and up the ankle, then tucked. They go on before anything else does, and they are what stops a stiff sole taking the skin off.

objects.name: Sackcloth
objects.desc: Coarse cloth woven from whatever fibre came to hand, loose enough to see daylight through. It sacks grain, and at a push it clothes a body.

objects.name: Buckskin Leggings
objects.desc: Buckskin cut long and laced up the outside of the calf, soft enough to kneel and hold still in.

objects.name: Elk-Leather Greaves
objects.desc: Heavy elk leather over the shin, cut with a slit behind the knee so a stalker can still crouch.

objects.name: Owlbear-Leather Greaves
objects.desc: Thick owlbear leather, still ridged where the beast's own muscle lay under it.

objects.name: Hippogriff-Feather Greaves
objects.desc: Feathered hide laid down the shin with the quills running to the ankle, so rain sheds off it.

objects.name: Linen Trousers
objects.desc: Linen hose, pointed to a belt and cut close so nothing catches on a stirrup.

objects.name: Quilted Linen Trousers
objects.desc: Stuffed and stitched the length of the thigh, heavy and hot, and worth both when a spear comes low.

objects.name: Rune-Woven Trousers
objects.desc: Hose of the same close spiral as the robe, weightless and cold to the touch.

objects.name: Copper Scale Gloves
objects.desc: Small copper scales laced over a leather glove, leaving the palm bare to grip with.

objects.name: Copper Scale Shoes
objects.desc: Scaled flaps over the instep, laced under the sole. They turn a stamped foot and little else.

objects.name: Steel Gauntlets
objects.desc: Articulated steel over the back of the hand, the fingers lamed in strips so they still close on a grip.

objects.name: Steel Sabatons
objects.desc: Overlapping steel lames down the foot, hinged at the toe. Loud on stone, and worth it.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Gauntlets
objects.desc: Alloy plates cut with the same close script as the cuirass, warm to hold even in the cold.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Sabatons
objects.desc: Graven lames over the foot that ring faintly when the wearer stops walking.

objects.name: Iron Buckler
objects.desc: A fist-sized iron disc held out on a bar grip. It cannot hide behind — it is swung at the incoming edge to knock it aside.

objects.name: Steel Heater Shield
objects.desc: A tall steel-faced shield tapering to a point below the knee, strapped along the whole forearm. Nothing gets past it and nothing about it is quick.

objects.name: Rune-Graven Kite Shield
objects.desc: Alloy laid over a long kite frame and cut with script from boss to point. Blows land on it and go quiet.

objects.name: Goblin Scrap Helm
objects.desc: A cook-pot with the handle knocked off and a strap riveted through it. It has been someone else's twice.

objects.name: Goblin Bark Bracers
objects.desc: Slabs of bark bound over the forearms with stolen cord, the inside still smelling of the tree.

objects.name: Goblin Ring Vest
objects.desc: A hauberk cut off at the ribs to fit something half the size, the raw edge left to rust.

objects.name: Goblin Pot Helm
objects.desc: Riveted iron scraps with eye-slots hacked through, worn over a filthy cap.

objects.name: Kobold Scale Vest
objects.desc: Overlapping scutes stitched to a hide backing, cut narrow across the chest. It fits nothing taller than a child.

objects.name: Kobold Delver's Helm
objects.desc: A hide cap with a stub of tallow candle still lashed above the brow.

objects.name: Kobold Bone Bracers
objects.desc: Split rib bone laid along the forearm and whipped tight with sinew.

objects.name: Gnoll Bone Harness
objects.desc: Ribs and shoulder blades lashed across the chest in a rough lattice, still yellowed at the joints.

objects.name: Gnoll Skull Helm
objects.desc: The upper skull of something with a long jaw, hollowed and strapped under the chin.

objects.name: Gnoll Hide Greaves
objects.desc: Untrimmed hide wrapped from ankle to knee, tied with gut.

objects.name: Orc Horned Helm
objects.desc: A thick iron pot with two hacked-off horns riveted at the temples, packed out with rags.

objects.name: Orc Iron Greaves
objects.desc: Bands of iron hammered around the shin over stinking hide. They were not measured for anyone.

objects.name: Orc Warhelm
objects.desc: A full iron helm with a slot for the eyes and a chin bar, blackened by whatever fire forged it.

objects.name: Orc Plate Greaves
objects.desc: Slabs of plate strapped over the thigh, dented inward more often than out.

objects.name: Branch Bracers
objects.desc: Straight sticks laid side by side along the forearm and whipped tight. Turns a claw once.

objects.name: Branch Greaves
objects.desc: Split branches bound down the shin, rattling with every step. Nothing about this is quiet.

objects.name: Bark Sandals
objects.desc: Slabs of bark cut to the shape of a foot and held on with plaited cord between the toes. They wear through in a season and cost nothing but an afternoon.

objects.name: Roast Joint
objects.desc: A whole joint set in the banked heat of a masonry hearth and left to turn slowly in its own fat. The outside darkens and crusts while the middle stays pink.

objects.name: Baked Fish
objects.desc: Whole fish laid on hot stone with herbs pushed into the belly, baked until the skin lifts away clean.

objects.name: Baked Roots
objects.desc: Roots buried in the embers of a spent fire and left overnight. They come out sweet and collapsing, skins blackened.

objects.name: Bone Stock
objects.desc: Bones and trimmings held at a bare simmer for a day and a night, until the marrow gives up and the liquor sets to jelly when cold.

objects.name: Braised Game
objects.desc: Tough cuts shut in a covered pot with stock and root vegetables and left on a low corner of the stove until a spoon goes through them.

objects.name: Seared Steak
objects.desc: A thick cut dropped onto iron hot enough to spit, turned once, and rested. The crust is the point.

objects.name: Fresh Sausage
objects.desc: Meat and fat chopped coarse, seasoned hard and filled into casings, then fried through on the plate. Eaten the same day.

objects.name: Confit
objects.desc: Salted meat cooked for hours in its own fat at a heat too low to brown it, then packed into a crock and sealed under a finger of white fat. It keeps through winter.

objects.name: Feast Platter
objects.desc: Everything the kitchen can do, sent out on one board — a carved joint, sausage, confit and bread, with the roots underneath soaking up the drippings and a wheel of cheese and a jug of wine going round after it.

objects.name: Wine-Poached Fish
objects.desc: A baked fish lifted off the bone and set back over a low flame under wine and herbs until the liquor goes clear. Light enough to eat slowly and still get up afterwards.

objects.name: Cold Milk Soup
objects.desc: Stock let down with milk and stood in the coldest corner of the house until it is barely warmer than the well. More drunk than eaten, and the only thing anyone wants at noon in high summer.

objects.name: Marching Loaf
objects.desc: A loaf opened at the top, hollowed out and packed hard with confit and cheese, then closed and weighted overnight. It goes into a pack whole and comes out in slices days later.
